## Thesis

PT Esa Medika Mandiri (EMMI) is a >20-year independent distributor of medical, laboratory and pharmaceutical devices — carrying global principals including Medtronic, Medicon, Bowa, Penlon and Air Liquide — with two light-manufacturing factories (Cikupa, Solo). The defining fact is concentration: roughly **96% of revenue (96.1% in 2025) goes to the government**, and an even higher **98.5% of gross profit**. Recent growth has been explosive but lumpy and margin-dilutive, funded by a heavily-geared balance sheet. The IPO is 100% primary, raising mostly working capital. It prices at a demanding trailing P/E, and a pre-IPO land revaluation has cosmetically improved how the leverage reads. This is a higher-risk name than its headline growth implies.

## How the business works

EMMI is, in substance, a single operating company — the parent — with a cluster of near-zero subsidiaries (EBT, MMM, SUN, SSN, EWI) consolidated in 2023, contributing between 0.003% and 0.929% of revenue. It wins government and multilateral tenders, pre-funds the inventory and project goods, delivers, then carries long government receivables. There are **no long-term sales contracts** (a stated risk), so revenue is inherently lumpy. The 2024 surge was driven by specific named tenders rather than recurring demand: **IsDB (Islamic Development Bank) tenders of Rp47.4 bn** and a **World Bank SOPHI tender of Rp101.7 bn, of which only ~20% (~Rp20 bn) was recognised in 2025**. That leaves ~Rp81 bn of SOPHI revenue still to recognise — genuine near-term visibility — but beyond the current backlog, earnings depend entirely on winning fresh tenders, and a budget cut, lost tender or payment delay hits ~96% of the business.

## The offering & ownership

The company offers **522,857,000 new shares (30% of post-IPO capital, all primary)** at **Rp446–Rp515** (par Rp50), with no selling shareholders and no greenshoe. Underwriting is full-commitment by **PT BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (lead) and PT INA Sekuritas Indonesia** — a credibility step up, with both declaring no affiliation to the issuer. The "Ina" overlap with lender Bank Ina Perdana is coincidental: INA Sekuritas is the former Nikko Sekuritas Indonesia, unrelated to Salim-group Bank Ina Perdana, so there is no underwriter-lender conflict.

Critically, there is **no statutory POJK 25/2017 founder lock-up**: the prospectus states no party acquired shares below the IPO price in the six months before registration, so the current structure (set by Akta No. 153, 23 Feb 2026) is treated as predating the window. The only restraint is Surya Gunawan Widjaja's **12-month commitment to retain control (≥50%)** — which permits selling down toward 50%. The founder block is in principle freely tradable from listing day; this entire position hinges on the capital history genuinely predating the window and warrants verification. The **ESA** allots up to **52,285,700 shares (10% of offered / 3% post-IPO)**, including "Saham Penghargaan" reward shares carrying a notably long **30-month lock-up**.

## Governance & related parties

All owners are individuals — no holding company. Surya Gunawan Widjaja is the declared controller (UBO), and the Widjaja family holds 85% pre-IPO falling to 59% post-IPO. The governance item worth a careful read: the **Independent Commissioner is a former senior Ministry of Health (Kemenkes) medical-device regulator** — per the disclosed CV, Director of Medical Device & PKRT Assessment (2021–2024) and Director of Medical Device Supervision (2016–2021), now also leading a medical-device industry association. This is reproduced factually with no inference of wrongdoing. Analytically it cuts both ways: deep regulatory and tender expertise for a 96%-government supplier, against weakened substance of "independence" for a recent regulator of the exact products EMMI sells. Related-party items include **building rental income of Rp2.61 bn (2025)** and a **joint venture contributing equity-method profit of Rp4.10 bn (2025)** — roughly 12% of net profit, non-core income that flatters the bottom line and whose counterparty and durability merit confirmation.

## Reading the financials

The trajectory is striking but qualified. Sales grew **+122.5% in 2024 and +18.1% in 2025 to Rp454.64 bn**, but the 2024 surge came with a **gross-margin collapse from 51.3% to 35.3%** (35.9% in 2025) — this is low-margin government volume, not premium product. Leverage is the second story: **interest expense (Rp30.44 bn in 2025) consumed 247% of operating profit in 2023 and still 46% in 2025**, the signature of a debt-funded model. Note that 2025 net profit attributable to parent (**Rp34.13 bn**) exceeds total profit (Rp32.44 bn) because non-controlling interests absorbed Rp1.69 bn of subsidiary losses — EPS must be struck on parent profit.

Working capital is structurally stretched: the **current ratio was below 1.0 in every year (0.48× / 0.82× / 0.92×)**, with government receivable days lengthening to **110 in 2025**. The structural item to flag is the **Rp37.65 bn land revaluation** of the Serpong HQ in 2025 — independently appraised and proper under PSAK 16, but **non-cash**. It lifted equity from Rp73.4 bn to Rp145.0 bn and **cut reported liabilities/equity from 8.74× to 2.89×** right before the IPO. Strip it out and DER is ~3.91× — the deleveraging is partly cosmetic, since the cash debt did not fall; the equity denominator was revalued up. The FY2024/2023 comparatives were also **restated (*disajikan kembali*)**, superseding the earlier reports — the restatement reason should be read in the notes.

## Valuation

At the range, the post-IPO market cap is **Rp777.3 bn–Rp897.6 bn**, putting EMMI on a **~22.8×–26.3× trailing P/E** on 2025 parent profit. That is demanding for a ~96% government-concentrated, ~7% net-margin, heavily-leveraged, tender-dependent distributor — you are paying a growth multiple for earnings whose visibility past the SOPHI/IsDB backlog is low. Quality caveats compress the case: ~12% of net profit is JV equity income, book value (and therefore P/BV) is flattered by the land revaluation, and ROE drops to ~8.5% once the equity base roughly doubles post-raise. The land revaluation makes P/BV *look* cheaper; stripping it out, it is not. Natural live comparables are IDX-listed med-device names IRRA and OMED, whose current multiples should be pulled at publication date before any relative cheap/expensive judgement.

## Bottom line

EMMI offers real growth, a genuine sector tailwind (≈8.68% market CAGR to 2030, plus JKN and TKDN support), credible principals, better underwriting than recent small-cap peers, and ~Rp81 bn of SOPHI backlog for near-term visibility. Against that sits a concentrated and fragile core: ~96% government revenue with no recurring contracts, heavy leverage (interest at 46% of operating profit), chronic negative working capital, margin-dilutive growth, a book value and leverage profile flattered by a pre-IPO revaluation, no hard founder lock-up, and a demanding ~23–26× P/E. The structure is sensible for the working-capital engine it funds, but the margin of safety is thin — returns hinge on tender win-rate and collection discipline, and the risks run deeper than the headline growth suggests.

# IPO Forensic Analysis — PT Esa Medika Mandiri Tbk (Ticker: **EMMI**)

> **Source document:** *Prospektus Awal* (Preliminary Prospectus), 346 pages, issued 22 June 2026. FY2025 financials audited by **KAP Mirawati Sensi Idris (member of the Moore Global network)**, **unmodified opinion**, report dated 15 June 2026, signed Emanuel Handojo Pranadjaja CA, CPA (AP.0929). **FY2024/2023 comparatives were RESTATED (*disajikan kembali*)** — the pre-restatement reports (dated 3 Dec 2025 and 25 Jul 2025) were superseded. See §6 and §7.4.
> **Analyst note (method):** preliminary prospectus → price is a *range*, issuance-cost lines are "[*]%". Where I quantify net proceeds it is **back-solved from the prospectus's own allocation arithmetic** (caveated), not a heuristic. No stale peer multiples are used. Prepared for presentation use (Kang Ritel / kupas-prospektus); opinions are labelled as analysis and attributed to the prospectus, UU ITE-aware (documented facts only, no allegations).

---

## 0. Executive Snapshot

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Issuer | PT Esa Medika Mandiri Tbk (HQ Esa 8 Building, Gading Serpong, Tangerang) — ~20+ yrs in the business |
| Ticker | **EMMI** (IDX), sector Healthcare — **medical-device / lab / pharma DISTRIBUTION + light manufacturing** |
| Core business | Independent distributor of medical/lab/pharma devices (principals incl. Medtronic, Medicon, Bowa, Penlon, Air Liquide) + 2 factories (Cikupa, Solo); **~96% of revenue is to GOVERNMENT** |
| Shares offered | **522,857,000 new shares** = **30%** of post-IPO capital (100% primary) |
| Price range | **Rp446 – Rp515** (par Rp50) |
| Gross proceeds | **Rp233.2 bn (floor) – Rp269.27 bn (cap)** |
| Implied net proceeds | **≈ Rp256.4 bn at cap** (back-solved → implied *biaya emisi* ≈ 4.8% of gross; see §3.1) |
| Post-IPO market cap | **Rp777.3 bn – Rp897.6 bn** (1,742,857,000 shares) |
| Underwriters | **PT BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (lead) + PT INA Sekuritas Indonesia** — *full commitment*. **Higher-tier than the Sucor deals (JELI/PRDL)** |
| Controlling shareholder | **Surya Gunawan Widjaja (30% → 21%)**; Widjaja family 85% → 59% post-IPO; Eddy Lie 15% → 10% |
| Ultimate Beneficial Owner | **Surya Gunawan Widjaja** (declared controller) — all shareholders are individuals, no holding company |
| Lock-up | **No statutory POJK 25/2017 founder lock-up applies** (prospectus claims no below-IPO-price acquisitions in the 6-mo window) — only a 12-month control commitment. **Weak, like JELI** |
| ESA | Yes — up to 52,285,700 shares (10% of offered / 3% post-IPO); reward shares carry a **30-month lock-up** |
| Subsidiaries | 5 (EBT, MMM, SUN, SSN, EWI) — **all tiny or dormant** (0.003–0.929% of revenue) |
| Dividend | See §7.4 (confirm policy/history in Bab XI) |
| Indicative timeline | Bookbuilding 22–24 Jun · OJK effective 30 Jun · Public offer 2–6 Jul · Listing **8 Jul 2026** |
| 2025 revenue / net profit | Rp454.6 bn (**+18.1% YoY**, after +122.5% in 2024) / **Rp34.13 bn** attrib. parent (+210% YoY) |

**One-line thesis:** A fast-growing but **~96% government-dependent**, **thin-margin (gross 36%)**, **heavily-leveraged (interest = 46% of operating profit)**, **working-capital-negative (current ratio <1 every year)** medical-device distributor whose recent growth came from **lumpy multilateral tenders (IsDB, World Bank SOPHI)** rather than recurring revenue. The IPO funds working capital (68.7%) and partial debt repayment. A **Rp37.65 bn land revaluation** (independently appraised, but timed for IPO) cut reported leverage from 8.74× to 2.89× and inflated book value. Priced at a **demanding ~23–26× trailing P/E**. Better underwriting (BRI Danareksa) and a real sector tailwind, but the government concentration + leverage + tender-lumpiness make this a higher-risk name than the headline growth suggests.

---

## 1. Current Shareholders & Ownership Chain

### 1.1 Pre- and post-IPO cap table (par Rp50)

- **All natural-person owners — no holding company** (unlike JELI's NUI or PRDL's Prodia Utama). The **Widjaja family holds 85% pre-IPO / 59% post-IPO**; with Eddy Lie aligned, 69% post-IPO. **Surya Gunawan Widjaja** is the declared **controller (PSP)**.
- Authorised capital 4,300,000,000 shares (Rp215 bn). The current structure was set via Akta No. 153 (23 Feb 2026), two days before registration (25 Feb 2026) — relevant to the lock-up question (§4).

### 1.2 Board — governance flag worth a careful read
> ⚠️ **The Independent Commissioner is a former senior Ministry of Health medical-device regulator.** Per the disclosed CV, this commissioner (appointed 2026) previously served at the **Ministry of Health (Kemenkes)** as **Director of Medical Device & PKRT Assessment (2021–2024)**, Director of Medical Device Supervision (2016–2021), and acting director roles in pharmaceutical/medical-device resilience and public-drug governance (2020–2022) — and now also leads a medical-device industry association. **This is the documented prospectus disclosure; I draw no inference of wrongdoing.** Analytically it cuts two ways: (i) **bull** — deep regulatory expertise and government/tender access for a company selling ~96% to government; (ii) **governance optics** — a recent senior regulator of the exact products EMMI sells, seated as the *independent* commissioner shortly after leaving office, weakens the substance of "independence" and creates conflict-of-interest optics. A sophisticated reader should weigh this; present it factually, not accusatorially (UU ITE).

---

## 2. Affiliations with the Existing Stock Market & Related Parties

### 2.1 Capital-market affiliations
- **No listed-affiliate parent** (unlike PRDL↔PRDA). EMMI is independently family-held; this would be the family's first listed vehicle.
- **Underwriters: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (lead) + INA Sekuritas Indonesia.** Both declare **no affiliation with the issuer** (Bab XIII–XIV). BRI Danareksa is the IB arm of state-bank BRI — a credibility step up from the Sucor small-cap deals.
- 🔎 **Fact-check (cleared):** EMMI repays debt to **Bank Ina Perdana**, and a co-underwriter is **PT INA Sekuritas**. The "Ina" name overlap is **coincidental** — **PT Ina Sekuritas is the former PT Nikko Sekuritas Indonesia** (an Indonesia–Japan JV since 1990, renamed 2023), **unrelated to Bank Ina Perdana** (Salim group). **There is no underwriter-lender conflict here.** (Flagged and dismissed so the wrong inference isn't drawn.)
- **Listed competitors named in the prospectus:** **PT Jayamas Medica Industri (OMED)** and **PT Itama Ranoraya (IRRA)** — the natural live comparable set for valuation (§8).

### 2.2 Related parties (per the financial statements)
- **Building rental income** (Rp2.61 bn in 2025) and a **joint venture** (*ventura bersama*) contributing **equity-method profit of Rp4.10 bn (2025)** / Rp1.63 bn (2024); JV carrying value Rp5.73 bn. The JV profit is ~12% of 2025 net profit — non-core, equity-method income that flatters the bottom line; identify the JV counterparty and its sustainability.
- Confirm the full related-party transactions note (Bab VIII / financial-statement notes) for any sales/purchases with Widjaja-family entities; the subsidiaries (below) were brought into the group in 2023 (a pre-IPO consolidation).

### 2.3 Subsidiaries — mostly tiny or dormant
| Sub | Business | Owned | Rev contribution 2025 | Status |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| EBT | Wholesale lab/pharma/medical devices | 60% | 0.003% | Operating (Solo factory) |
| MMM | General trading/construction/services | 55% | – | Operating |
| SUN | Retail+wholesale lab/pharma/medical devices | 90% | 0.929% | Operating (Cikupa factory) |
| SSN | Not yet operating | 99% | – | Dormant (est. 2024) |
| EWI (indirect via SSN) | Not yet operating | 55% | – | Dormant (est. 2024) |

> **Read-through:** the "Grup" is effectively **one operating company (the parent)** with a cluster of near-zero subsidiaries gathered in 2023. Consolidation adds little revenue but does introduce NCI (which absorbed Rp1.69 bn of losses in 2025 — see §6).

---

## 3. Public Offered Shares, Proceeds & Red Flags

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Shares offered | 522,857,000 (all **new/primary**) |
| % of post-IPO capital | 30.00% |
| Price range | Rp446 – Rp515 (par Rp50) |
| **Gross proceeds** | **Rp233.2 bn → Rp269.27 bn** |
| Selling shareholders | None |
| Greenshoe | None disclosed |
| Issuance-cost % | "[*]%" (blank) — net back-solvable, §3.1 |

### 3.1 Proceeds & Net (back-solved from the prospectus's own math)
Item 1 (debt) is a **fixed Rp50.0 bn**; items 2–3 are **11.8% + 68.7% = 80.5% of net** → debt = 19.5% of net → **net proceeds ≈ Rp50.0 bn ÷ 0.195 ≈ Rp256.4 bn** (at cap). Against gross Rp269.27 bn that implies **biaya emisi ≈ Rp12.9 bn ≈ 4.8% of gross** — reasonable for a deal this size (cheaper % than PRDL's tiny deal). *Caveat: assumes the percentages were computed at the cap-price scenario; at the floor (gross Rp233.2 bn) the fixed Rp50 bn debt repayment absorbs a larger share.*

### 3.2 Red flags / structuring notes
1. 🟠 **Working-capital-dominated use of proceeds (68.7%).** The bulk of the raise funds **inventory + project-related goods + receivables**, not productive assets — the signature of a thin-margin, project-based distributor. Returns depend on working-capital efficiency and continued tender wins; it does not build durable earning capacity the way a factory would.
2. 🟠 **~19.5% (Rp50 bn) repays bank debt** (Bank Ina Perdana, partial) — a partial deleveraging of a heavily-geared balance sheet; substantial debt remains (§6).
3. 🟡 **Capex (11.8%) builds the Cikupa factory** — modest; the company is primarily a distributor, not a manufacturer.
4. 🟡 **Mid-cap, but the price (Rp446–515) is a real number** (not gocap) — the cover still flags **share illiquidity** as the secondary risk; 30% free float at ~Rp0.78–0.90 tn market cap is investable but small.

## 4. Lock-up, ESOP & ESA

### 4.1 Lock-up — **weak (like JELI, not PRDL)**
- The prospectus invokes POJK 25/2017 but states **no party acquired shares below the IPO price within the 6 months before registration**, therefore **no statutory lock-up binds the founders.** The current shareholding (Akta No. 153, 23 Feb 2026) is treated as predating the window (a par re-split, not a fresh below-price issuance). **→ The 70%/85% founder block is, in principle, freely tradable from listing day.**
- The only restraint is **Surya Gunawan Widjaja's 12-month control commitment** (≥50%). As with JELI, "not relinquishing control" ≠ "not selling" — he can sell down toward 50% and still comply.
- ⚠️ **Verify in Bab VIII (capital history)** that the founder shares genuinely predate the 6-month window (par Rp50 vs IPO Rp446–515 — any recent at-par issuance *would* trigger the lock-up). The entire "no lock-up" position hinges on this, exactly as it did for JELI.

### 4.2 ESA
- Up to **52,285,700 shares (10% of offered / 3% post-IPO)**. Comprises fixed-allotment shares and **"Saham Penghargaan" (reward shares) with a 30-month lock-up** (notably long vs PRDL's 12 months) — better retention alignment. Confirm the split between employee-paid and company-funded (free) portions and quantify any cash/P&L cost.

The IPO essentially **recapitalises the working-capital engine** and trims interest cost — sensible for the model, but it means equity holders are funding the float, and returns hinge on win-rate and collection discipline.

> 🚩 **Two red flags.** (1) **Current ratio < 1 in every year (0.48 / 0.82 / 0.92)** — current liabilities *exceed* current assets throughout; the company chronically funds working capital with short-term liabilities. ## 10. Bull vs. Bear

**Bull case**
- Real, fast growth (sales +122.5% in 2024, +18.1% in 2025); ~Rp81 bn SOPHI backlog gives near-term visibility.
- Genuine sector tailwind (health budget, JKN, TKDN, ~8.7% market CAGR); credible global principals (Medtronic et al.).
- **Better underwriting (BRI Danareksa)** than the Sucor small-caps; long 30-month ESA lock aligns staff; deep government/regulatory know-how on the board.

**Bear case**
- **~96% government concentration**, **tender-lumpy** revenue, **no recurring contracts**; **heavy leverage** (interest 46% of operating profit); **chronic negative working capital**.
- Margin-dilutive growth (gross 51%→36%); **book value/leverage flattered by a pre-IPO land revaluation**; **no hard founder lock-up**; **demanding ~23–26× P/E**.
- Governance optics (ex-regulator as "independent" commissioner); FY2024/2023 restated.

forensicMd:
## Thesis

PT Prodia Diagnostic Line Tbk (PRDL, brand Proline) is a small, founder-controlled in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturer inside the Prodia group, raising roughly Rp62 bn at the cap by issuing 522,900,000 new primary shares (30.00% of post-IPO capital) at Rp100–Rp120 per share. The defining feature is *what the money is for*: the IPO is primarily a debt-repair exercise, with a fixed Rp35,666,666,667 — the majority of net proceeds — earmarked to repay bank debt taken on for a 2024 capacity build that collided with a revenue collapse. This is effectively a second IDX listing of the Prodia group, alongside the already-listed PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA). The analytical read is that PRDL is cheap in absolute terms (~10–12× trailing P/E, ~1.4× P/BV) but that discount is *earned*: extreme earnings volatility, severe channel concentration, a pre-IPO restatement and auditor change, and a thin, illiquid float.

## How the business works

PRDL manufactures IVD reagents and diagnostic instruments (clinical chemistry, hematology, immunology, biomolecular) under the Proline and DiaSys brands, classified under KBLI 21015. It is a standalone single entity with no subsidiaries, so net profit equals owner profit with no minority interest. Crucially, it is not a captive intra-group sales channel: it sells overwhelmingly through third-party distributors and OEM partners rather than to the Prodia lab network, which is structurally cleaner on the revenue side but concentrates risk in that external distributor channel. Distribution reaches roughly 370 kabupaten/kota and 7,600+ end-users (hospitals, puskesmas, public and private labs), with a small workforce of 81 (2025). The revenue mix is shown in a separate card.

## The offering & ownership

This is a 100% primary offering — all 522,900,000 shares are newly issued, with no selling shareholders and no disclosed greenshoe. Because the issuance-cost line is blank ("•%") in the preliminary prospectus, net proceeds are *back-solved* from the prospectus's own allocation arithmetic — the fixed Rp35.667 bn debt item equals 62.57% of net, implying net proceeds of roughly Rp57.0 bn at the cap and a biaya emisi near 9.2% of gross. Price sensitivity is severe and asymmetric: since debt repayment is a fixed Rupiah amount, a weak book at the floor would push it to ~76.6% of net, squeezing growth (capex plus working capital) to roughly Rp11 bn. Ownership stays firmly with the founder group — Prodia Utama and PRDA together hold ~63% post-IPO, with Diasys at 7%; the cap table is a separate card.

## Governance & related parties

Control rests collectively with six Prodia founders (each 16.67% of Prodia Utama), the same group that controls listed PRDA — so this is a group monetisation/restructuring, not an independent company; cross-reading PRDA's disclosures is warranted, as is verifying the named Independent Commissioner's genuine independence given the tight control. The pivotal relationship is the *triple dependency on Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH (Germany)*: simultaneously a 10%-pre / 7%-post shareholder, the technology licensor, and a reagent/raw-material supplier. The licence (since April 2011, recently extended 13 April 2026 to 17 April 2033) lets PRDL manufacture reagents under Diasys supervision for licence fees; the Euro-denominated payable (Rp628 m at YE2025) confirms ongoing purchases. The extension de-risks the near term, but core reagent technology resting on one foreign related party is a structural risk, and working-capital proceeds may partly flow back to Diasys. Other related-party links are mostly cost-side (notably renting its building from Grhanis); related-party *revenue* is immaterial.

## Reading the financials

The headline 2025 result — revenue Rp74.37 bn (+26.8%) and net profit Rp16.99 bn (+69.9%) — must not be read off a cherry-picked base. 2023 is an anomalous peak (revenue +301.9%, profit +1,809%) that was ~77% driven by a single BUMN distributor, PT Rajawali Nusindo (Rp86.07 bn), almost certainly a government health-program order that did not repeat; when it collapsed, 2024 revenue halved (−47.5%) and profit fell −72.1%. Even the 2025 recovery leaves the business ~33% below its 2023 revenue peak, and Rajawali Nusindo remains ~33% of revenue (top-3 channels ~54%). This is the company's own stated #1 risk — dependence on lumpy government health spending — and it makes earnings inherently low-visibility. Meanwhile non-current assets roughly doubled to Rp148.9 bn on debt funding for the Cikarang build, cash collapsed 63% in 2025 to Rp10.8 bn, and DSCR fell to 1.95 in 2024 against a ≥1 covenant — the deleveraging rationale for the IPO. The structural quality item is the audit cluster: FY2025 carries an unmodified EY (KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja) opinion with revenue recognition as the Key Audit Matter, but FY2024/2023 were audited by a *different* firm (KAP HHES) and the FY2024 statements were *restated/reissued* (Emphasis of Matter). An auditor change (HHES→EY) stacked with a restatement of the very revenue line that is the KAM is the top diligence item; the restatement reason should be established before relying on a clean "audited by EY" line.

## Valuation

On an absolute basis PRDL is cheap — roughly 10–12× trailing earnings and ~1.4× book — the opposite of a premium deal. The analytical caution is that the discount is appropriate rather than an opportunity: the multiple is only as reliable as the assumed normal earnings power, and 2025's Rp16.99 bn, the 3-year average (~Rp20.9 bn), and the unrepeatable 2023 peak imply very different P/E lenses. Post-money ROE also compresses toward ~12% as equity roughly doubles. The natural live comparable is PRDA, its own listed affiliate, plus other IDX healthcare/med-device names — those current multiples should be pulled at publication before any relative cheap/expensive call. The full multiples table is a separate card.

## Bottom line

PRDL offers real positives that the structural story partly offsets: healthy gross margins (61–68%), the Prodia brand and listed-affiliate parentage, a Big-4 EY audit, the Diasys licence secured to 2033, a genuine government-health-spending tailwind (APBN 2026 health budget Rp244 tn; the CKG screening program), and — notably — a *materially stronger* lock-up than peers, with a hard 8-month POJK 25/2017 undertaking on all three pre-IPO holders (70% of post-IPO capital) plus a 12-month control commitment from the six UBOs. The ESA is generous and aligning but a real cash cost: up to 36,603,000 shares (7% of offered) given free to permanent staff, paid from internal cash, with a 12-month lock-up. Against that sits a debt-repair use of proceeds that leaves ~Rp58 bn of bank debt outstanding, volatile and government-dependent earnings off an unrepeatable peak, an unresolved 2024 restatement, capacity built ahead of demand, thin cash, and a tiny illiquid near-par float. The verdict is consistent throughout: cheap, but cheap for documented reasons.

narrativeMd:
# IPO Forensic Analysis — PT Prodia Diagnostic Line Tbk (Ticker: **PRDL** / "Proline")

> **Source document:** *Prospektus Awal* (Preliminary Prospectus), 348 pages, issued 18 June 2026. FY2025 financials audited by **KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja (member firm of Ernst & Young Global / EY Indonesia)**, **unmodified opinion** with a **Key Audit Matter (Hal Audit Utama) on REVENUE RECOGNITION**. FY2024/2023 comparatives were audited by a **different firm ("KAP HHES")** and **restated/reissued** (Emphasis of Matter). See §6 and §7.4 — the auditor change + restatement cluster is a core quality item.
> **Analyst note (method):** preliminary prospectus → price is a *range*, issuance-cost lines are "•%". Where I quantify net proceeds, it is **back-solved from the prospectus's own allocation arithmetic**, not a heuristic — and clearly caveated. Figures are in Rupiah; the audited statements are presented "dalam ribuan Rupiah" (thousands), converted here to billions. Prepared for presentation use (Kang Ritel / kupas-prospektus). Opinions are labelled as analysis and attributed to the prospectus; no defamatory inference (UU ITE-aware).

---

## 0. Executive Snapshot

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Issuer | PT Prodia Diagnostic Line Tbk — brand **Proline** (founded 16 Apr 2010 as *PT Dialine Systems Indonesia*; renamed 2011) |
| Ticker | **PRDL** (IDX), sector Healthcare / **In-Vitro Diagnostics (IVD)** manufacturing (KBLI 21015) |
| Core business | Makes IVD **reagents & instruments** (clinical chemistry, hematology, immunology, biomolecular) under *Proline*/*DiaSys* brands; sells mainly via third-party distributors |
| Shares offered | **522,900,000 new shares** = **30.00%** of post-IPO capital (100% primary) |
| Price range | **Rp100 – Rp120** per share (par **Rp50**) |
| Gross proceeds | **Rp52.29 bn (floor) – Rp62.748 bn (cap)** |
| Implied net proceeds | **≈ Rp57.0 bn at cap** (back-solved from the prospectus's own use-of-proceeds math → implied *biaya emisi* ≈ 9.2% of gross; see §3.1 — caveated) |
| Post-IPO market cap | **Rp174.3 bn – Rp209.1 bn** (1,742,900,000 shares) |
| Sole lead underwriter | **PT Sucor Sekuritas** — *full commitment* (same house running JELI; PRDL lists 9 Jul, JELI 7 Jul 2026) |
| Controlling shareholder | **PT Prodia Utama 51%** → 35.70% post-IPO |
| Other pre-IPO holders | **PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA — a *listed* company) 39% → 27.30%**; **Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH (Germany) 10% → 7.00%** |
| Ultimate Beneficial Owners | Six individuals (Prodia founders), each 16.67% of Prodia Utama: **Andi Widjaja, Gunawan Prawiro Soeharto, Haneke Suryadi, Justini Hidajat, Elisabeth Listijani W., Arjati Utami** |
| Lock-up | **8-month POJK 25/2017 lock-up on ALL three pre-IPO holders** + 12-month control commitment from the six UBOs — *stronger than JELI* |
| ESA | **Yes** — up to 36,603,000 shares (7% of offered), free ("cuma-cuma") to permanent staff, paid from internal cash, **12-month lock-up** |
| Dividend policy | Up to **20% payout** (lower than JELI's 30%) |
| Subsidiaries | **None** — standalone single entity |
| Indicative timeline | Bookbuilding 18–23 Jun · OJK effective 29 Jun · Public offer 1–7 Jul · Allotment 7 Jul · Listing **9 Jul 2026** |
| 2025 revenue / net profit | Rp74.37 bn (**+26.8% YoY**) / Rp16.99 bn (**+69.9% YoY**) — *but both far below the 2023 peak* |

**One-line thesis:** A small (Rp62 bn raise), founder-controlled IVD manufacturer inside the Prodia group, IPO-ing **primarily to repay bank debt (~63% of proceeds)** after a debt-funded capacity build collided with a **47% revenue collapse in 2024**. The 2023 "boom" was **~77% driven by a single BUMN distributor** (a government-channel order that did not repeat). Priced **cheaply in absolute terms (~10–12× trailing P/E, ~1.4× P/BV)** — appropriately, given extreme earnings volatility, customer concentration, a 2024 restatement, and a debt-repair use of proceeds. Real positives: EY audit, a genuine 8-month lock-up, healthy gross margins (61–68%), the Prodia brand/parentage, the Diasys technology licence (extended to 2033), and a structural government-health-spending tailwind (APBN 2026 Rp244 tn; free-health-check program).

---

## 1. Current Shareholders & Ownership Chain

### 1.1 Pre-IPO cap table (Akta No. 40, 6 Feb 2026; par Rp50)

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **PT Prodia Utama** | 622,200,000 | 31,110,000,000 | **51.00%** |
| **PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA — listed)** | 475,800,000 | 23,790,000,000 | **39.00%** |
| **Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH (Germany)** | 122,000,000 | 6,100,000,000 | **10.00%** |
| **Total** | **1,220,000,000** | **61,000,000,000** | **100.00%** |

Authorised capital is 4,880,000,000 shares (Rp244 bn). A par-value re-split to Rp50 and the current structure were set up in Feb 2026 for the IPO. *(Founding 2010 structure was different — Drs. Soesanto Natanael 45.2%, Dr. Hubertus Susilaganda Sutoyo 20%, PRDA 34.8%; the original individuals were bought out and Prodia Utama + Diasys came in.)*

### 1.2 Post-IPO cap table (cap price)

| Shareholder | Shares | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| PT Prodia Utama | 622,200,000 | **35.70%** |
| PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA) | 475,800,000 | **27.30%** |
| Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH | 122,000,000 | 7.00% |
| **Public (<5% each)** | 522,900,000 | **30.00%** |
| **Total** | **1,742,900,000** | **100.00%** |

### 1.3 Ownership chain & UBOs

```
Six individuals (Prodia founders), 16.6667% each of PT Prodia Utama:
  Andi Widjaja · Gunawan Prawiro Soeharto · Haneke Suryadi · Justini Hidajat · Elisabeth Listijani W. · Arjati Utami
        │  (collectively control)
        ▼
PT Prodia Utama  ──51%──┐
PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA, listed) ──39%──┼──►  PT Prodia Diagnostic Line (PRDL)  [no subsidiaries]
Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH (Germany) ──10%──┘
```

- **No single dominant controller** — Prodia Utama is owned in six equal 16.67% slices. Control is exercised collectively by the founder group (declared beneficial owners under Perpres 13/2018). Andi Widjaja (Dr. Andi Wijaya, the Prodia founder) is Komisaris Utama of Prodia Utama.
- **The same six individuals also control listed PRDA** (via Prodia Utama). So PRDL is effectively a **second listing from the same controlling group** — a group monetisation/restructuring, not an independent company.

### 1.4 Board
Read the full director/commissioner list in Bab VIII; the prospectus appoints an Independent Commissioner per POJK 33/2014. *(Verify the named Independent Commissioner's genuine independence given the tight founder control — same governance caveat as any closely-held IDX issuer.)*

---

## 2. Affiliations with the Existing Stock Market & Related Parties

This is the densest part of the PRDL story — and it cuts **both ways**.

### 2.1 Affiliation with a *listed* company (PRDA)
- **PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA)** — a company **already listed on IDX** (clinical-laboratory operator) — owns **39% pre-IPO / 27.30% post-IPO** of PRDL, and shares the same ultimate controllers (via Prodia Utama). This is a **direct affiliation with an existing listed issuer**. Implications: (i) cross-read PRDA's disclosures and trading history for context; (ii) potential for related-party flows between PRDL and the PRDA lab network; (iii) the group has prior public-market experience (a mild positive for disclosure discipline).
- **PT Prodia Utama** is the common parent of both PRDA and PRDL — a classic group "carve-out" listing.

### 2.2 The Diasys relationship (shareholder + licensor + supplier — triple dependency)
- **Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH** (Germany): 10% pre / 7% post-IPO shareholder, **AND** the **technology licensor**, **AND** a **reagent/raw-material supplier**.
- Licence & cooperation agreement since **April 2011**: PRDL is licensed to manufacture reagents under Diasys supervision, using the "DiaSys" trademark (or "Proline" for reagents made with Diasys-supplied raw materials), with training, QC inspection and method updates from Diasys; PRDL pays licence fees. Original term to 8 Jun 2026; **extended 13 Apr 2026 to 17 Apr 2033**.
- ⚠️ **Dependency flag:** PRDL's core reagent technology rests on a single foreign related party that is also a shareholder. The recent extension (to 2033) de-risks the near term, but a non-renewal/dispute at term, or a change in Diasys's terms, is a structural risk. The related-party trade *payable* to Diasys (in Euro, Rp628 m at YE2025) confirms ongoing reagent purchases. Working-capital IPO proceeds may partly flow to Diasys (related party) for raw materials — disclosed as an affiliated transaction under POJK 42/2020.

### 2.3 Other related parties (mostly on the COST side — important)
Related-party **revenue is immaterial** (related-party trade receivables were only **2.0% (2023) / 3.7% (2024) / 7.6% (2025)** of total trade receivables). The Prodia network is **not** a captive sales channel. Related parties identified:

| Related party | Relationship | Nature of transactions |
|---|---|---|
| Diasys Diagnostic Systems GmbH | Shareholder | Inventory purchases, freight, **licence fee** |
| PT Prodia Distribusi Medika | Other related party | Sales & purchases of inventory; rental income; *other receivable Rp1.49 bn (99% of other receivables) in 2025* |
| PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA) | Other related party / shareholder | Sales & delivery of services; other operating expense |
| PT Innovasi Diagnostika | Other related party | Sales & purchases of inventory |
| PT Grhanis Prima Propertindo | Other related party | **Building maintenance expense** |
| PT Grhanis Putra Propertindo | Other related party | **Building rental expense** |

> **Read-through:** PRDL **rents its building from a related party** (Grhanis) and **buys core reagents/licence from a related party** (Diasys), but **sells mostly to third parties**. That is structurally *cleaner* on the revenue side than a captive intra-group model (less transfer-pricing/circular-revenue concern) — but it concentrates the risk in the third-party distributor channel (§3 red flags) and leaves cost-side related-party dependencies (Diasys, Grhanis) to monitor.

### 2.4 Capital-market affiliation of underwriter/professionals
- **PT Sucor Sekuritas** (sole lead, full commitment) — the same house running the JELI IPO two days earlier. Confirm the prospectus's affiliation declaration (Bab XII–XIII) states no affiliation with the issuer.

---

## 3. Public Offered Shares, Proceeds & Red Flags

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Shares offered | 522,900,000 (all **new/primary**) |
| % of post-IPO capital | 30.00% |
| Price range | Rp100 – Rp120 (par Rp50) |
| **Gross proceeds** | **Rp52.29 bn → Rp62.748 bn** |
| Selling shareholders | None |
| Greenshoe | None disclosed |
| Issuance-cost % | "•%" (blank in draft) — but net is back-solvable, see §3.1 |

### 3.1 Proceeds & Net (back-solved from the prospectus's own math)
Unlike JELI, PRDL's use-of-proceeds lets us **derive net proceeds from disclosed figures** rather than estimate: item 1 (debt) is a **fixed Rp35,666,666,667**, and items 2–3 are **28.92% + 8.51% = 37.43% of net**. Therefore debt = 62.57% of net → **net proceeds ≈ Rp35.667 bn ÷ 0.6257 ≈ Rp57.0 bn**. Against gross of Rp62.748 bn (cap), that implies **biaya emisi ≈ Rp5.75 bn ≈ 9.2% of gross** — high, but plausible for a sub-Rp65 bn deal where fixed costs (legal/audit/listing/printing) are a larger percentage.

> **Caveat (state on slide):** this back-solve assumes the percentages were computed at the **cap-price** scenario. At the **floor** (gross Rp52.29 bn), if rupiah costs are similar (~Rp5.75 bn), net ≈ Rp46.5 bn — and because **debt repayment is a fixed Rp35.67 bn**, it would absorb **~76.6% of net**, squeezing capex+WC to ~Rp11 bn. **Price sensitivity is severe** and asymmetric: a weak book hits the *growth* portion hardest.

### 3.2 Red flags / structuring notes
1. 🔴 **This is a debt-repair IPO, not a growth IPO.** ~63% of net proceeds (Rp35.67 bn) repays bank debt (BCA fully + ~Rp14.2 bn of Panin). Only ~28.9% capex + ~8.5% working capital funds growth. Investors are substantially **bailing out a leveraged balance sheet**, not funding expansion.
2. 🔴 **Even post-IPO the company stays leveraged.** Total bank debt at YE2025 ≈ **Rp94.3 bn**; repaying Rp35.67 bn leaves **~Rp58 bn outstanding** (mostly Panin). This is *partial* deleveraging.
3. 🟠 **Tiny float in rupiah terms** (Rp52–63 bn) at a **near-par price (Rp100–120 vs Rp50 par)** — the classic IDX small-cap "gocap-adjacent" profile, which the prospectus itself flags via **illiquidity as the secondary risk**. Expect thin liquidity and high aftermarket volatility (auto-reject dynamics common in this segment).
4. 🟡 **Media data discrepancy:** some outlets (Kompas/Kontan) quoted the debt repayment as "~Rp33.66 bn"; the prospectus states **Rp35,666,666,667**. Use the prospectus figure.

---

## 4. Lock-up, ESOP & ESA

### 4.1 Lock-up — *materially stronger than JELI*
- **All three pre-IPO shareholders** (PRDA 19 Feb, Prodia Utama 20 Feb, Diasys 24 Feb 2026) signed **POJK 25/2017 statements not to sell/transfer ANY shares for 8 months** after the effective date. So unlike JELI, there **is a hard 8-month lock-up on 100% of pre-IPO shares** (70% of post-IPO capital).
- Additionally, the **six individual UBOs** (Andi Widjaja, Gunawan Prawiro Soeharto, Justini Hidajat, Elisabeth Listijani W., Arjati Utami, Haneke Suryadi) committed (Apr 2026) **not to relinquish control for 12 months**.
- *Verify in Bab XVII whether the 8-month statement is the statutory POJK 25/2017 lock-up (triggered by below-IPO-price acquisitions within 6 months pre-registration) or a broader voluntary undertaking; either way, the practical effect — no founder selling for 8 months — is a genuine positive vs. JELI's no-hard-lock structure.*

### 4.2 ESA (Employee Stock Allocation) — exists, and it's a cash cost
- Up to **36,603,000 shares (7% of offered)**, exercise price = offer price, **given free ("cuma-cuma") to permanent employees** (≥12 months' tenure as of 30 Jun 2026, good-standing, good performance), **paid by the company from internal cash** to the underwriter. **12-month lock-up** on ESA shares.
- 💸 **Cost to the company:** 36.6 m × Rp100–120 = **Rp3.66–4.39 bn** of internal cash — that is **~22–26% of 2025 net profit** distributed as an employee bonus, spread over ~55 permanent employees (~Rp67–80 m each). Generous; it is a real P&L/cash cost and modestly dilutive of the cash that could otherwise reduce debt. Note it favourably (alignment/retention) but quantify the cost.
- No separate MESOP/option program disclosed.

> 🚩 **The 2023 figure is an anomaly, not a baseline.** Revenue +301.9% (so 2022 was only ~Rp27.8 bn) and net profit +1,809% — then a 47.5%/72.1% collapse in 2024. The 2025 "recovery" (+26.8% revenue, +69.9% profit) is real but leaves the business **~33% below its 2023 revenue peak and ~53% below peak profit**. **Do not headline the +69.9% profit growth** without the 2023→2024 collapse beside it — the cherry-picked base flatters the story.

### 6.2 The volatility driver — single-distributor (BUMN) concentration
From the significant-agreements disclosure, revenue by major channel:

| Distributor / channel | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **PT Rajawali Nusindo (BUMN distributor)** | **Rp86.07 bn** | Rp25.58 bn | Rp24.49 bn |
| — as % of total revenue | **~77.0%** | ~43.6% | ~32.9% |
| PT Sumbermitra Agungjaya | Rp12.46 bn | Rp9.82 bn | Rp7.65 bn |
| PT Visi Trading (OEM) | — | Rp4.14 bn | Rp8.16 bn |
| **Top-3 named, 2025** | | | **~Rp40.3 bn ≈ 54%** |

> 🔴 **This is the single most important finding.** The 2023 boom was **~77% a single BUMN distributor (Rajawali Nusindo)** — almost certainly a government health-program channel order (JKN / disease-control / screening) that **did not repeat**. When it fell ~70% in 2024, total revenue halved. Even in 2025, Rajawali Nusindo is ~33% of revenue and the top-3 channels are ~54%. **Severe customer/channel concentration + dependence on lumpy government procurement** = the prospectus's own #1 stated risk ("ketergantungan terhadap belanja pemerintah pada sektor kesehatan"). Earnings are inherently low-visibility.

- **Non-current assets ~doubled (Rp66.6 → 148.9 bn)** over 2023–25, **debt-funded** (long-term liabilities jumped from Rp46.7 bn in 2023 to Rp97.3 bn in 2024). The Cikarang facility build.
- **Cash collapsed 63% in 2025 (Rp29.5 → 10.8 bn)** — the company drew down liquidity servicing debt and funding the build into a soft-demand year. Low cash (Rp10.8 bn) is itself a reason the IPO/deleveraging is needed now.
- **DSCR fell to 1.95 in 2024** — thin debt-service cover, close to the covenant floor (≥1) and D/E (1.78) near the ≤2 limit. The IPO repayment restores headroom.

### 6.4 Audit quality — the cluster to scrutinise
- **FY2025:** audited by **EY Indonesia (KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja)** — Big-4, a step up from JELI's mid-tier auditor. Opinion **unmodified**. **Key Audit Matter = revenue recognition** (entirely appropriate given the volatility/concentration). The 2025 report was also **reissued** (Other Matter).

The restatement *reason* is not spelled out in the summary I reviewed — **this is the top diligence item.** It could be benign (reclassification, IPO-driven presentation alignment) or substantive (an error correction in the very revenue line that is the KAM). **Do not publish a clean "audited by EY" line without first reading the full EY/HHES reports and the restatement note** to establish what was restated and why.

## 7. Additional Useful Information

### 7.1 Business profile
- **IVD manufacturer (KBLI 21015)** under brand **Proline**: clinical chemistry, hematology, immunology and biomolecular **reagents + diagnostic instruments**. Core reagent tech licensed from **Diasys (Germany)** since 2011.
- **Customers:** 7,600+ end-users (hospitals, puskesmas, government & private clinical labs); distribution reaches **370 kabupaten/kota**. Management claims runway: ~47% of health facilities and ~38% of district health offices are **not yet** customers.
- **Distribution channels** are third-party distributors (Rajawali Nusindo — BUMN; Sumbermitra) and OEM (Visi Trading); also a quality agreement with Shenzhen Dymind (China) and supply relationships with Mindray, Robert Riele, MiCo BioMd, Maccura. A KFTD (Kimia Farma) distribution arrangement is also referenced.
- **Workforce:** small — **81 (2025)** vs 74 (2024) vs 70 (2023); 55 permanent / 26 contract.

### 7.2 Industry tailwind (the bull case)
- APBN 2026 health budget **Rp244 tn** (up from Rp218.5 tn in 2025). The government **Cek Kesehatan Gratis (CKG)** program (~Rp2.6 tn, 13 screening types) — PRDL targets **~Rp2.2 tn addressable** for 9 screening types it already produces. Structural diagnostics demand + import-substitution policy support is the genuine growth thesis. (It is also the source of the *concentration/lumpiness* risk — the same coin, two sides.)

### 7.3 Auditor / opinion → see §6.4. **EY (FY2025), restated FY2024 under prior auditor HHES.**

### 7.4 Dividend
- Policy: up to **20% of net profit** (vs JELI 30%), subject to RUPS; not legally binding. Given the post-IPO debt load and capex plans, **near-term cash dividends are likely minimal**. Confirm dividend history in Bab XI.

### 7.5 Legal & covenants
- Debt covenants met at YE2025 (DSCR 2.81 / current 2.14 / D-E 1.34); no covenant breaches or payment defaults disclosed; no negative covenants harmful to public shareholders. Confirm the litigation section (clean standing) in the legal opinion (Bab XVII).

### 7.6 Key risk factors (per prospectus)
1. **Primary: dependency on government health spending** (the cover's stated #1 risk) — directly maps to the Rajawali Nusindo/BUMN-channel concentration.
2. **Share illiquidity** (small float, near-par price, single underwriter).
3. Single-supplier/licensor dependency on **Diasys** (foreign, related party).
4. Raw-material/FX (EUR/USD reagent imports), regulatory (medical-device licensing, BPOM/Kemenkes), product-quality/recall risk.

## 10. Bull vs. Bear

**Bull case**
- Real structural tailwind: rising government health budget (Rp244 tn) + CKG screening program (~Rp2.2 tn addressable); import-substitution policy favours a domestic IVD maker.
- Strong gross margins (61–68%); cheap absolute valuation (~10–12× P/E, ~1.4× book).
- Credible parentage (Prodia group, listed PRDA) + EY audit + Diasys technology (extended to 2033).
- **Genuine 8-month lock-up** on all founder shares (better than JELI); ESA aligns staff; post-IPO deleveraging restores covenant headroom.

**Bear case**
- **Debt-repair IPO**; earnings are **volatile and government/single-distributor dependent**; 2023 peak unrepeatable; business still below peak.
- **2024 restatement + auditor change** with revenue recognition as the KAM — unresolved.
- Capacity built ahead of demand; ~Rp58 bn debt remains; cash thin; tiny illiquid float.

1. **Why was 2024 restated?** Read the EY and HHES reports + the restatement note. Was the revenue-recognition KAM the cause? This is the #1 item.
2. **Q1-2026 revenue/order book** — is the government channel (Rajawali Nusindo / CKG) re-accelerating, or is 2025's ~Rp74 bn the run-rate?
3. **Exact Panin facility terms** (size, rate, maturity) and the precise post-IPO residual debt and pro-forma interest expense.

5. **Diasys economics** — licence-fee rate, raw-material pricing, exclusivity, and renewal terms to 2033.
6. **Utilization rate** of the new Cikarang capacity (undisclosed) and the realistic CKG-program revenue ramp.
7. **Live comparable multiples** (PRDA + IDX healthcare/med-device) at publication date for the relative-valuation call.

forensicMd:
## Thesis

RANS (PT RANS Entertainmen Indonesia Tbk) is a celebrity-IP media holding company built around Raffi Ahmad and Nagita Slavina, raising up to Rp429.25bn for 20.02% in a 100% primary offering. The bull case is a genuine, hard-to-replicate brand moat (one of Indonesia's largest social-media audiences) attached to a clean, almost debt-free balance sheet, with proceeds aimed at growth rather than repair. The bear case is in the trailing numbers: revenue has declined three years running and net profit fell 42% in 2025, while the deal is priced at a demanding ~28-35x earnings. This is a bet that the brand can re-accelerate a softening top line, paid for at a premium multiple, with the entire equity story resting on two people.

## How the business works

RANS monetises the audience and brand of Raffi Ahmad, Nagita Slavina and family across two audited segments. The Hiburan & Lifestyle segment (about 70% of FY2025 revenue and the profit engine, at roughly 35% segment margin) earns from social-media content and advertising, brand-ambassador and endorsement deals, talent management, a production house, and live events and ticketing. The Penjualan Produk segment (about 30%) sells IP-branded food, beverage and beauty products, and was loss-making in 2025 (a segment loss of around Rp12bn). The defining dependency is key-person concentration: revenue and brand value are tied to the continued involvement and reputation of Raffi and Nagita, which the issuer names as its own number-one risk. The demand backdrop is a large, young, social-first Indonesian consumer base, but the asset being sold is fundamentally the reach and goodwill of a single family.

## The offering & ownership

The IPO is 2,525,000,000 new shares (20.02% of post-IPO capital), entirely primary, so all proceeds accrue to the company. Pricing is Rp135 to Rp170 (par Rp10), implying a post-IPO market capitalisation of roughly Rp1.70tn to Rp2.14tn on 12,609,250,000 shares, underwritten on a full-commitment basis by Trimegah. Ownership is concentrated: Raffi Farid Ahmad holds 62.93% post-IPO as sole controller and ultimate beneficial owner, with the founder and family bloc (nine pre-IPO holders including Nagita Slavina, Dony Oskaria, Soultan Ariq Rachman and Kaesang Pangarep) at 79.98% against a 20.02% public float. The lock-up is genuinely strong: all nine pre-IPO holders signed 8-month statutory POJK 25/2017 lock-up statements, and Raffi has separately committed to retain control for three years. There is no ESA or MESOP programme. Dividend policy is up to 35% of net profit starting FY2026.

## Governance & related parties

Control and economic ownership are aligned in one person, which removes the control-mismatch question seen in some peers but raises the opposite concern: minority influence is minimal under a single ~63% controller. The use of proceeds carries the related-party item to watch. About 19.8% of the raise (Rp85bn) funds an acquisition tied to the Slavina/family brand, and a further slice funds an AI joint venture (Feedloop) and the Cipungland project, so a meaningful portion of public money flows into ventures within the founder's orbit; the arm's-length basis and independent valuation of these should be confirmed in the final prospectus. The board's independent-commissioner substance and the related-party framework around content and endorsement deals (where the controller is also the product) are the governance areas a careful reader should weigh. The issuer reports a clean legal record.

## Reading the financials

The trajectory is the crux. Revenue declined each of the last three years, from Rp437.8bn (2023) to Rp410.5bn (2024) to Rp353.4bn (2025). Reported net profit looks like it rose then fell sharply, but the 2024 figure is flattered: it includes a one-off Rp44.9bn gain on the disposal of a subsidiary (the RPKSB sports business), offset by a Rp10.5bn loss from that discontinued operation, leaving total profit for the year of Rp97.1bn. Strip the disposal out and the underlying earnings trend is softening rather than growing; 2025 total net profit of Rp56.7bn is down about 42%. Note that profit attributable to parent (Rp61.0bn in 2025) exceeds total profit because non-controlling interests absorbed losses, so valuation should use the parent figure. The balance sheet, by contrast, is a real strength: total liabilities of Rp120.2bn against equity of Rp340.8bn put DER at just 0.35x (down from 0.62x in 2023), interest cover is roughly 20x, and the only interest-bearing debt is a single BNI investment facility (about Rp37bn) that the IPO largely retires. This is a low-leverage, cash-generative business; the question is top-line direction, not solvency.

## Valuation

At the range, RANS prices at roughly 27.9 to 35.1x trailing FY2025 earnings attributable to parent (about 30 to 38x on total profit), with post-money price-to-book near 2.3 to 2.8x. That is a demanding multiple to pay for a company whose revenue has fallen three years running and whose 2024 profit was inflated by a non-recurring disposal. The multiple only makes sense if the brand-led growth plan (concerts, the Slavina acquisition, IP products, the AI venture) genuinely reignites the top line and the Product segment turns. Pre-money ROE of 16.6% dilutes to roughly 8% post-raise as the equity base expands. Note that issuance costs and the proforma equity table are blank in this preliminary draft, so net proceeds and exact post-money book value are back-solved and should be confirmed. A relative read needs live multiples for Indonesian media and IP peers at publication.

## Bottom line

RANS pairs a rare asset, a durable celebrity-IP brand on a clean, low-leverage balance sheet, with an awkward financial profile and a full price. The 100% primary, growth-oriented structure and the strong lock-up are points in its favour, and the deleveraging is almost incidental because there is little debt to repay. Against that sit three years of declining revenue, a 42% profit drop once the 2024 disposal gain is set aside, a loss-making product arm, related-party uses of proceeds, and a ~28-35x multiple. The entire thesis reduces to one question: can the Raffi and Nagita brand convert reach into re-accelerating, recurring revenue, and is that worth paying a premium for while the trailing line still points down. Underwrite it only if you believe the brand re-rates the growth, not the history.

ownership.summary: RANS is a founder-controlled media holding (Raffi Ahmad 62.93% post-IPO, with wife Nagita Slavina) carrying unusually dense political exposure: the controlling owner is himself a sitting Presidential Special Envoy, while the register also includes SOE regulatory chief Dony Oskaria and PSI chairman Kaesang Pangarep (son of ex-President Jokowi). It is simultaneously conglomerate-linked through Emtek/SCMA (PT Indonesia Entertainmen Grup ~7.2% plus Emtek CEO Sutanto Hartono) and the listed Bali United group. A celebrity-and-politically-connected float where governance, related-party and headline risk weigh heavily.
flags: Controlling UBO Raffi Ahmad is a sitting government official (Presidential Special Envoy)

Emtek/SCMA conglomerate affiliation via PT Indonesia Entertainmen Grup and CEO Sutanto Hartono, implying related-party content/distribution dependence
Float is small (~20%) with the founder retaining majority control
caveats: Media-reported money-laundering allegations (2023-24) and an incidental mention in a 2026 customs trial never resulted in Raffi Ahmad being named a suspect, charged, or convicted; noted as headline-volatility risk, not a finding of wrongdoing.
October 2025 media reports described a wave of RANS staff resignations citing heavy workloads; sourced to ex-employee accounts, not a formal labor ruling.
Minority holder Hikmat Janika (0.68%) could not be reliably identified; one outlet's 'hospital official' identification may be a namesake. Confirm against the final prospectus.

narrativeMd:
# RANS — PT RANS Entertainmen Indonesia Tbk

Celebrity-IP media holding built around Raffi Ahmad and Nagita Slavina. Upcoming IDX IPO (listing 10 Jul 2026), lead underwriter Trimegah.

- **Offering:** 2,525,000,000 new shares (100% primary) = 20.02% of post-IPO capital. Par Rp10, price Rp135–170, gross up to Rp429.25bn. Post-IPO shares 12,609,250,000.
- **Control:** Raffi Farid Ahmad 62.93% (sole controller & UBO); founder/family bloc 79.98%; public 20.02%. 8-month statutory lock on all 9 pre-IPO holders; 3-year control commitment. No ESA.
- **Business:** Hiburan & Lifestyle (~70% of revenue: content, endorsements, talent, production, events) + Penjualan Produk (~30%: IP-branded F&B and beauty, loss-making in 2025).
- **Financials (audited, full Rp):** Revenue 437.8bn (2023) → 410.5bn (2024) → 353.4bn (2025), declining three years. Net profit (total) 84.4 / 97.1 / 56.7bn; 2024 flattered by a Rp44.9bn one-off disposal gain. DER 0.62 / 0.36 / 0.35 — low leverage.
- **Use of proceeds:** growth-led — concerts 37.6%, Slavina acquisition 19.8%, Cipungland capex 18.6%, Feedloop AI JV 8.2%, BNI debt 7.0%, RNS subsidiary ~8.8%.
- **Valuation:** post-IPO cap Rp1.70–2.14tn; trailing P/E ~28–35x (parent); P/BV post-money ~2.3–2.8x; ROE 16.6% → ~8% post-money. Dividend up to 35% from FY2026.

See the structured cards and the full forensic writeup for the analysis. Figures from the preliminary prospectus (Prospektus Awal); issuance cost and proforma equity are blank in the draft, so net proceeds are back-solved.

valuation.verdict:
**Rich.** At Rp130 to 140 you pay about 100 times last year's profit for a company that did not earn one from operations.

- Trailing P/E of 97 to 105x (76 to 82x on the twelve months to February 2026). The prospectus's own peers trade near 10.6x earnings and 0.34x sales; SWAP asks 19 to 21x sales.
- FY2025 net profit of Rp1.4bn came entirely from writing back Rp5.3bn of GeNose inventory impairment. Without it, operations lost Rp2.2bn. Operating cash flow has been negative for three periods running and revenue fell 30%.
- Rp12bn of the Rp40bn raised (30%) repays loans from Yayasan UGM and GMUM, both affiliates of the controller.
- Market cap of Rp139 to 149bn against Rp7bn of revenue and Rp17bn of equity: 8x book before the money comes in, 2.3x after.

Bottom line: a research spin-out with real licences, priced like a profitable growth company. The price only makes sense if you ignore the operating line.

dividendPolicy: Starting from fiscal year 2025 onward, management intends to pay cash dividends of up to (sebanyak-banyaknya) 20% of net profit for the year, subject to results, cash flow, working-capital/capex/investment needs and RUPS approval (Pasal 71 UU PT). Dividends paid in Rupiah. No negative covenants restricting public shareholders. History: cash dividend Rp1,182,504,198 paid 2022-07-07; stock dividend Rp12,160,000,000 paid 2026-04-27 (the retained-earnings capitalisation).
primaryRisk: Distribution and marketing risk: SWAP's products are research outputs that require sustained clinician/distributor education before adoption; the prospectus ranks this as the risk most affecting business continuity (PAGE 43).
industryTailwind: Indonesia's medical-device market is growing about 8% a year (2024 to 2029) and the government is pushing import substitution (TKDN) for devices. The prospectus cites a global device-equipment market of USD 19bn in 2025 rising to USD 28bn by 2030 (Marketsandmarkets), and 626 registered device manufacturers competing locally (SIINas).

redFlags.text: Profit quality: FY2025 and FY2024 net profit (Rp1.42bn / Rp3.46bn) exist only because of Rp5.33bn / Rp6.70bn reversals of GeNose inventory impairment booked as other income; gross profit (Rp3.27bn) is below opex (Rp5.45bn) so the core business is loss-making. 2M-2026 net loss Rp571m. (PAGE 29, 425, 408)

Balance sheet dominated by legacy GeNose stock: gross raw-material inventory Rp38.0bn (Heprogama Rp37.6bn) vs annual revenue Rp7.1bn; net inventory Rp19.6bn = 62% of total assets even after a Rp21.5bn allowance; inventory is uninsured. (PAGE 407, 408)
Receivables: Rp11.9bn gross of which Rp11.29bn >90 days (GeNose sales to Farmalab, Rajawali Nusindo, Indofarma-in-bankruptcy); 94% provided, so any upside is speculative. (PAGE 406, 363-364)

Customer concentration contradicts prospectus text: Phapros 47.8% and Anugerah Prima Medika 19.0% of FY2025 revenue (88.8% top-2 in FY2024), while the prospectus claims 'no customer significantly dominates'. (PAGE 322, 423)
Undisclosed-in-narrative related-party revenue: UGM accounted for 36.2% of FY2025 revenue and 53.6% of COGS (near pass-through), not shown in the 'pelanggan utama' table. (PAGE 426)

Governance concentration: UGM controls 99.93% pre-IPO via GMUM/direct/RSGM (~69.7% post-IPO at 30.3% float); Komut is a serving UGM Dean and Komisaris is GMUM's President Director; only one independent commissioner, no independent director; audit committee formed 28 May 2026 with no meetings yet. (PAGE 59, 293, 295-298, 302)

Operational dependence on the controller: factory buildings and some machinery are UGM property under a 5-year lease that UGM can terminate for 'strategic needs' on 3 months' notice; core IP is UGM/inventor-owned and licensed at 5%/15% royalties. (PAGE 172, 314, 109, 160-161)

Proceeds to affiliates: Rp12bn of ~Rp40bn net use of proceeds (30%) repays UGM-group lenders — Rp10bn to Yayasan UGM (loan taken only Feb 2026 to buy land) and Rp2bn to GMUM (GeNose-era loan not due until 2030). (PAGE 20, 21, 22)

Land for the Rp10.7bn new building is still titled to a third party, 65% of it is protected sawah under a conversion moratorium, and PBG is pending; construction not before Q2 2027. (PAGE 19, 20, 365, 366)
Tiny scale and shrinking: 57 staff, revenue -30% to Rp7.1bn in FY2025 on lower Venindo sales; herbal unit sells only Rp57m/yr. (PAGE 35, 310, 322)
Valuation: at Rp130-140 the company itself computes PER 228-246x, PBV 8.0-8.6x, PS 21-23x vs peer averages 10.6x / 1.4x / 0.34x. (PAGE 328, 329)

Full regulatory stack for a company this size: CPAKB, CDAKB, ISO 13485:2016, CPOTB Full Aspek, ISO 22000, halal; 13+ Kemenkes AKD device licences (PAGE 64, 65, 69-75, 313, 326)
Clean legal record: no litigation, disputes or somasi; unmodified audit opinion; labour compliance (BPJS, UMP, LKS Bipartit) (PAGE 313, 364-365)
Balance sheet: no bank debt; liabilities are affiliate loans (Rp8.3bn GMUM at 9.1% to 2030, Rp10bn YUGM at 3%), with Rp12bn to be repaid from IPO; equity Rp17.3bn (PAGE 24, 25, 29, 21, 22)

Distribution agreements in place with Phapros (state pharma group) and ~20 other distributors/hospitals; own CDAKB distribution unit IMEDEV (PAGE 178-260, 321)

openQuestions: What is the Rp2.58bn of FY2025 revenue sold to UGM itself (36% of sales at roughly 20% gross margin): a one-off project, or something that recurs?
Excluding the impairment write-backs, what is the run-rate operating loss and cash burn, and how many years does the Rp15.8bn working-capital allocation buy?
What is the Rp37.6bn of Heprogama raw-material inventory physically, what is it worth today, and why was Rp12bn of impairment reversed over two years on stock the prospectus calls unsellable?
Why does the prospectus say no customer dominates when Phapros alone is 48% of FY2025 revenue and the top two were 89% in FY2024?

What drove the ventilator sales collapse in 2025, and is there an order book for 2026?
After the IPO, GMUM's remaining Rp6bn loan at 9.1% stays on the books. With negative operating cash flow, how is it serviced?
Final offer price and issuance cost are blank in the draft. At the Rp140 ceiling, gross proceeds exceed the Rp40bn plan by Rp5bn. Where does the surplus go?
Will UGM add an independent director or a second independent commissioner, and what will management be paid after listing (the board drew nothing in 2024, 2025 and early 2026)?

forensicMd:
## Thesis

SWAP is not a company selling Rp7bn of medical devices at 100 times earnings. It is Universitas Gadjah Mada floating 30% of its research-commercialisation vehicle to raise Rp40bn, of which Rp12bn flows straight back to UGM-side lenders, at a price the prospectus's own peer table cannot justify. The headline net profit (Rp1.42bn in FY2025) exists only because Rp5.33bn of GeNose-era inventory impairment was reversed into other income; strip that out and the business lost Rp2.2bn at the operating line, burned cash in every period, and posted a net loss in the first two months of 2026. Everything an investor is asked to pay for — the pedigree, the licences, the pipeline — belongs to the university, not the listed entity.

## How the business works

The company was founded in 2012 as UGM's engine for turning faculty research into products. Three units sit inside the UGM Science Technopark in Kalasan, Sleman: Heprogama (medical devices — the INA-SHUNT hydrocephalus shunt, GAMA-CHA bone graft, Ceraspon haemostatic sponge, Venindo ventilators, RZ-VAC negative-pressure wound device), Gamafood (wedang and cookies), and Gama Herbal Indonesia. Devices were 80.3% of FY2025 revenue, food 18.9%, herbal 0.8%. Fifty-seven people work there, thirty-one of them in production; the board and directors drew no remuneration in 2024, 2025 or early 2026.

The intellectual property is licensed, not owned. Patents, industrial designs and the core trademarks sit with UGM and carry a 5% royalty on annual sales (Rp894m in FY2025, Rp1.19bn in FY2024); the INA-SHUNT know-how belongs to its inventor, who takes 15% royalty plus a 15% R&D contribution. The buildings are UGM's too, leased for five years with a clause letting the university reclaim them on three months' notice for "strategic needs". SWAP itself owns twenty trademarks, two motorcycles, one Innova, and its lab and production equipment.

Sales run through a handful of counterparties. PT Phapros distributed 47.8% of FY2025 revenue and PT Anugerah Prima Medika 19.0% (the top two were 88.8% in FY2024). Separately, the financial-statement related-party note shows UGM itself bought Rp2.58bn of product in FY2025 — 36.2% of revenue — at close to pass-through cost, a line that appears nowhere in the prospectus's "major customers" narrative, which claims no customer dominates. The revenue trend is down: Rp10.21bn in 2024 to Rp7.12bn in 2025 as ventilator demand faded, with FY2023 not presented at all. Management's growth story rests on distributor expansion, new devices (a stent, an EVD, a neonatal ventilator) and contract manufacturing; no order book or capacity figures are disclosed.

## The offering & ownership

Up to 323,000,000 new shares — 100% primary — at Rp130–140, par Rp20, for 30.30% of a 1,066,000,000-share company. Gross proceeds Rp41.99–45.22bn against a use-of-proceeds plan that totals exactly Rp40.0bn "net of costs", so the ceiling price leaves Rp2–5bn unexplained. The lead is PT Sukadana Prima Sekuritas, the renamed OSO Sekuritas, on a full-commitment basis, with no joint underwriters named and fees left blank. No ESA, no warrants. The filing runs under POJK 53/2017 as a small-asset issuer (total assets Rp31.8bn at 28 February 2026).

Post-IPO, PT Gama Multi Usaha Mandiri holds 67.72% and UGM 1.88% directly — 69.60% under one roof, since GMUM is 98.63% owned by the university. The prospectus names the sitting Rector, Prof. dr. Ova Emilia, as the controlling party by RUPS resolution, while the ownership section describes the controller as the institution acting through its Rector. Both readings lead to the same place: the controller is an office whose occupant changes by appointment (the current term ends in 2027), and UGM's undertaking not to relinquish control lasts only twelve months from the effective date. Two other holders, PT Radio Swaragama and CEO Bondan Ardiningtyas, own 0.05% each. All four pre-IPO holders sit under the eight-month POJK 25/2017 lock because the April 2026 Rp12.16bn stock dividend and Rp1,000-to-Rp20 split fell inside the six-month window.

## Governance & related parties

The board is a UGM board. The Komisaris Utama is the Dean of UGM's Faculty of Economics and Business; the second commissioner is GMUM's President Director; the one independent commissioner joined in 2026 and chairs an audit committee formed in May 2026 that had not yet met. Neither of the two directors is independent. The CEO is a UGM pharmacist who ran the university's clinic and pharmacy for fourteen years and is a named inventor on some of the licensed IP.

Money moves in every direction between the company and its controller. UGM is licensor (5% royalty), landlord (Rp1.51bn over five years, reclaimable), customer (36% of FY2025 sales), and, through GMUM, lender: a Rp8.27bn shareholder loan at 9.10%, originally raised to accelerate GeNose C19 production and extended to December 2030, with profit-sharing clauses on GeNose still attached. Yayasan UGM added a Rp10bn loan at 3% in February 2026 to fund the land purchase for the new building. The IPO's debt-repayment allocation — Rp12bn, 30% of net proceeds — repays Yayasan UGM in full and GMUM in part. The prospectus discloses each of these as a related-party transaction with the amounts; what it does not do is add them up — Rp12bn of the Rp40bn raised from the public is earmarked to repay the controller's own affiliates.

The legal opinion is clean on litigation but lists open items an operating company would prefer closed: the new-site land is still titled to its seller and 65% of it is protected rice paddy under a conversion moratorium; no spatial-use confirmation (PKKPR) exists for the production site because Sleman is revising its RTRW; a groundwater permit is pending; several BPOM food and herbal licences are in renewal, one having expired in August 2026.

## Reading the financials

The income statement has two layers and only one of them is a business. Revenue fell 30% to Rp7.12bn in FY2025; gross profit of Rp3.27bn (46% margin) did not cover Rp5.45bn of operating expenses, leaving an operating loss of Rp2.18bn (Rp1.04bn in 2024). The company reported net profit of Rp1.42bn (Rp3.46bn in 2024) because it reversed Rp5.33bn (Rp6.70bn) of impairment previously taken on GeNose raw materials and booked it as other income. Excluding those reversals, pre-tax losses were Rp2.75bn and Rp1.6bn. The audited two months to 28 February 2026 show revenue up 28% to Rp589m, gross margin collapsing to 17.8%, and a net loss of Rp571m. Operating cash flow was negative in every period presented (−Rp1.6bn, −Rp3.4bn, −Rp2.3bn for the two months) and cash fell from Rp7.3bn to Rp1.3bn.

The balance sheet is a monument to GeNose. Gross inventory is Rp41.1bn against Rp7.1bn of annual sales; even after a Rp21.5bn allowance, net inventory of Rp19.6bn is 62% of total assets and is uninsured. Receivables of Rp11.9bn gross are 94% provided because the counterparties — Farmalab, Rajawali Nusindo, Indofarma — are post-PKPU or bankrupt. A Rp7.2bn deferred-tax asset rounds out the soft assets. Equity was Rp17.9bn at year-end 2025; total-liabilities-to-equity 0.87 (0.24 pro forma post-IPO), and there is no bank debt — every rupiah of borrowing is from the UGM family. The open question the prospectus never answers is why management reversed Rp12bn of impairment across two years on stock it elsewhere describes as unsellable after the pandemic.

## Valuation

At Rp130–140 the company is worth Rp138.6–149.2bn. On the FY2025 net profit that is 97.5–105× trailing earnings; on the twelve months to February 2026, 76–82×; on earnings excluding the impairment reversals there is no multiple because there are no earnings. Price-to-sales is 19.5–21×. Price-to-book is 8.0–8.6× on today's equity and 2.26–2.43× on the pro-forma post-money equity of Rp61.4bn; return on equity goes from 7.95% reported to roughly 2.3% post-money. The prospectus's own peer set — OMED and IRRA — trades near 10.6× earnings, 1.4× book and 0.34× sales, and its own valuation table prints 228–246× on a different (unreconciled) earnings base. Whichever number one prefers, the gap is not a premium for growth; revenue shrank.

## Bottom line

This is a research-institute spin-out with real certifications, a credible device pipeline and no litigation, priced as if it were a profitable growth company. The profit is accounting, the cash flow is negative, the inventory is a pandemic relic, the customers are two distributors plus the parent, and a third of the money raised goes back to the parent's lenders. The underwriter's only recent lead IPO (OBAT, 2025) popped and then fell a third below its offer price. There may be a case for owning UGM's commercialisation arm at a fraction of this valuation once the GeNose balance sheet is written down and the core business shows it can cover its own overhead. At Rp130–140, with a tiny float and a grade-C sponsor, the day-one trade and the long-run investment are different questions — and the second one is answered by the operating line, not the net line.

ownership.summary: SWAP is controlled by a state university, not a family or a conglomerate. UGM holds about 69% after the IPO through its business arm GMUM plus a small direct stake, and the prospectus names the sitting Rector as the controlling party. That control changes hands by statute: the Rector's term ends in 2027, within a year of listing, and UGM's undertaking not to give up control runs only twelve months. The university is also licensor (5% royalty on the core products), landlord (a lease it can reclaim on three months' notice), customer (36% of FY2025 revenue) and, through GMUM and Yayasan UGM, lender; Rp12bn of the proceeds repays those two. We rate the exposure mixed: not PEP-linked, because the Rector's public-official status is institutional rather than political, and not clean, because so much of the company's IP, premises and funding sits with the controller.

business.summary: SWAP is UGM's research-commercialisation vehicle: a tiny Sleman (Yogyakarta) manufacturer of research-based health products operating from leased buildings inside the UGM Science Technopark. It runs three production units — Heprogama (medical devices: INA-SHUNT hydrocephalus shunt, GAMA-CHA bone graft, Ceraspon haemostatic sponge, Venindo ventilators, RZ-VAC wound therapy, Divabirth), Gama Herbal Indonesia (traditional-medicine capsules/sprays) and Gamafood (wedang uwuh, herbal teas, gluten-free cookies, sambal) — plus an in-house distribution unit IMEDEV. Most core products are licensed from UGM patents/marks against a 5% royalty on sales. FY2025 revenue was only Rp7.1bn (down 30% from Rp10.2bn) and the company was loss-making at the operating line; reported net profit exists only because of reversals of legacy GeNose inventory impairment.

business.breakdown_basis: Sales by business unit/segment (PAGE 322 table; FS note 19 PAGE 423). Table header says 'dalam jutaan Rupiah' but figures are full Rupiah. Percentages computed by me from the Rp figures.
business.model: Own-brand manufacturer of UGM research outputs. IP is mostly not owned: core devices/herbals are produced under UGM patent/mark/design licences with a 5% royalty on annual sales paid to UGM (split UGM 40% / inventor unit 20% / inventor 40%), and INA-SHUNT under a direct partnership with inventor Sudiharto paying 15% royalty plus 15% R&D contribution (net of tax, on selling price). Products are sold B2B through IMEDEV (own distribution licence) and third-party distributors (Phapros for INA-SHUNT, Anugerah Prima Medika, Sukses Bumi Medika, Andini Sarana, Natur Ace, Global Systech Medika) to public/private hospitals, clinics and labs, on term-of-payment credit. Management also pitches contract manufacturing / teaching-factory services and KSO as future revenue lines, but these are not yet material. Pricing not disclosed beyond distributor agreements.

key_customers_or_channel.concentration_note: Top-2 customers = 66.8% of FY2025 and 88.8% of FY2024 revenue (FS note 19). Separately, FS note 23 shows revenue from PTN BH UGM of Rp2.58bn = 36.23% of FY2025 revenue (vs 0.44% in 2024), with matching COGS to UGM of Rp2.06bn (53.6% of COGS) — apparently a low-margin pass-through project. UGM is not listed in the prospectus 'pelanggan utama' table, and the prospectus text claims 'no customer dominates', which the numbers contradict.

moat_or_edge.assessment: Edge is institutional (UGM pedigree) rather than proprietary: patents sit with UGM/inventors, buildings and some equipment belong to UGM, and the company says there is no reliable data on its market position.

business.capacity_and_utilization: Not quantified. Prospectus only states management currently occupies ~12 rooms in Gedung B UGM STP alongside production, so production space 'cannot be optimised'; the new Rp10.7bn building (distribution centre + office) is meant to free that space. No unit capacity or utilisation figures are given.

rd_and_ip.ip_ownership: Patents/industrial designs/marks for the core products are owned by UGM (Spons Hemostatik Sintetis patent, NPWT patent, Divabirth industrial design, sexual-dysfunction pharmaceutical patent, Asilact and AG Fit marks, GamaCHA) and licensed to SWAP; INA-SHUNT know-how belongs to inventor Sudiharto (SWAP pays patent maintenance costs). SWAP owns only 20 trademarks.
rd_and_ip.royalties: 5% of annual product sales to UGM per licence (late-payment penalty 1 permil/day, max 5%); 15% royalty + 15% R&D contribution to Sudiharto for INA-SHUNT. Royalty expense: Rp1.19bn FY2024, Rp894m FY2025, Rp64.5m 2M-2026 (FS note 21). Royalty payments in cash flow: Rp1.17bn 2024, Rp978m 2025.
rd_and_ip.rd_spend: No separate R&D expense line; R&D is done with UGM faculties (Fitofarmaka Ocimum project, heat-resistant omega-3 chocolate, secretome stem-cell cream MoU) and via LPPT UGM lab-affiliation agreement. IPO working capital earmarks Rp1bn for cardiac stent, EVD and neonatal ventilator development.

business.demand_backdrop: Demand for the legacy Covid product (GeNose) collapsed after the pandemic, leaving ~Rp37.6bn of gross Heprogama raw-material inventory (Rp21.5bn provided) and ~Rp11bn of >90-day receivables. Ventilator (Venindo) sales fell in 2025, cutting revenue 30%. Management says there is no significant trend affecting the business since year-end, and pins growth on distributor expansion, new devices (stent, EVD, neonatal ventilator), herbal/food lines and contract manufacturing.
