valuation.flag: RICH - ~98-105x trailing FY2025 P/E (76-82x TTM) and ~19-21x P/S vs peer avg 10.6x P/E, 0.34x P/S, 1.36x PBV (prospectus' own table). Worse: FY2025 'profit' is a Rp5.3bn non-cash inventory write-back; ex-recovery the company runs an operating loss (-Rp2.2bn), CFO has been negative 3 periods running, revenue fell 30% in 2025, and 30% of net proceeds round-trips to UGM affiliates. The Rp138-149bn market cap prices a Rp7bn-revenue, cash-burning UGM spin-out at 8x book pre-money.
valuation.verdict:
**Rich.** At Rp130 to 140 you pay about 100 times last year's profit for a company that did not earn one from operations.

- Trailing P/E of 97 to 105x (76 to 82x on the twelve months to February 2026). The prospectus's own peers trade near 10.6x earnings and 0.34x sales; SWAP asks 19 to 21x sales.
- FY2025 net profit of Rp1.4bn came entirely from writing back Rp5.3bn of GeNose inventory impairment. Without it, operations lost Rp2.2bn. Operating cash flow has been negative for three periods running and revenue fell 30%.
- Rp12bn of the Rp40bn raised (30%) repays loans from Yayasan UGM and GMUM, both affiliates of the controller.
- Market cap of Rp139 to 149bn against Rp7bn of revenue and Rp17bn of equity: 8x book before the money comes in, 2.3x after.

Bottom line: a research spin-out with real licences, priced like a profitable growth company. The price only makes sense if you ignore the operating line.

raw.dividend_policy: Starting from fiscal year 2025 onward, management intends to pay cash dividends of up to (sebanyak-banyaknya) 20% of net profit for the year, subject to results, cash flow, working-capital/capex/investment needs and RUPS approval (Pasal 71 UU PT). Dividends paid in Rupiah. No negative covenants restricting public shareholders. History: cash dividend Rp1,182,504,198 paid 2022-07-07; stock dividend Rp12,160,000,000 paid 2026-04-27 (the retained-earnings capitalisation).
raw.primary_business_risk: Distribution and marketing risk: SWAP's products are research outputs that require sustained clinician/distributor education before adoption; the prospectus ranks this as the risk most affecting business continuity (PAGE 43).
raw.industry_tailwind: Indonesia's medical-device market is growing about 8% a year (2024 to 2029) and the government is pushing import substitution (TKDN) for devices. The prospectus cites a global device-equipment market of USD 19bn in 2025 rising to USD 28bn by 2030 (Marketsandmarkets), and 626 registered device manufacturers competing locally (SIINas).

red_flags.flag: Profit quality: FY2025 and FY2024 net profit (Rp1.42bn / Rp3.46bn) exist only because of Rp5.33bn / Rp6.70bn reversals of GeNose inventory impairment booked as other income; gross profit (Rp3.27bn) is below opex (Rp5.45bn) so the core business is loss-making. 2M-2026 net loss Rp571m. (PAGE 29, 425, 408)

Balance sheet dominated by legacy GeNose stock: gross raw-material inventory Rp38.0bn (Heprogama Rp37.6bn) vs annual revenue Rp7.1bn; net inventory Rp19.6bn = 62% of total assets even after a Rp21.5bn allowance; inventory is uninsured. (PAGE 407, 408)
Receivables: Rp11.9bn gross of which Rp11.29bn >90 days (GeNose sales to Farmalab, Rajawali Nusindo, Indofarma-in-bankruptcy); 94% provided, so any upside is speculative. (PAGE 406, 363-364)

Customer concentration contradicts prospectus text: Phapros 47.8% and Anugerah Prima Medika 19.0% of FY2025 revenue (88.8% top-2 in FY2024), while the prospectus claims 'no customer significantly dominates'. (PAGE 322, 423)
Undisclosed-in-narrative related-party revenue: UGM accounted for 36.2% of FY2025 revenue and 53.6% of COGS (near pass-through), not shown in the 'pelanggan utama' table. (PAGE 426)

Governance concentration: UGM controls 99.93% pre-IPO via GMUM/direct/RSGM (~69.7% post-IPO at 30.3% float); Komut is a serving UGM Dean and Komisaris is GMUM's President Director; only one independent commissioner, no independent director; audit committee formed 28 May 2026 with no meetings yet. (PAGE 59, 293, 295-298, 302)

Operational dependence on the controller: factory buildings and some machinery are UGM property under a 5-year lease that UGM can terminate for 'strategic needs' on 3 months' notice; core IP is UGM/inventor-owned and licensed at 5%/15% royalties. (PAGE 172, 314, 109, 160-161)

Proceeds to affiliates: Rp12bn of ~Rp40bn net use of proceeds (30%) repays UGM-group lenders — Rp10bn to Yayasan UGM (loan taken only Feb 2026 to buy land) and Rp2bn to GMUM (GeNose-era loan not due until 2030). (PAGE 20, 21, 22)

Land for the Rp10.7bn new building is still titled to a third party, 65% of it is protected sawah under a conversion moratorium, and PBG is pending; construction not before Q2 2027. (PAGE 19, 20, 365, 366)
Tiny scale and shrinking: 57 staff, revenue -30% to Rp7.1bn in FY2025 on lower Venindo sales; herbal unit sells only Rp57m/yr. (PAGE 35, 310, 322)
Valuation: at Rp130-140 the company itself computes PER 228-246x, PBV 8.0-8.6x, PS 21-23x vs peer averages 10.6x / 1.4x / 0.34x. (PAGE 328, 329)
Licensing/permit gaps: no PKKPR for the production site (RTRW revision), pending SIPA water permit with criminal exposure, several BPOM MD/TR licences in renewal. (PAGE 361-363)
Supplier payable concentration: Rp2.50bn of Rp2.51bn trade payables owed to one supplier (YPTI, ventilator hardware). (PAGE 24)
Legacy GeNose liability: Rp3.27bn 'utang lain-lain' to Indofarma Global Medika to be settled in RZ-VAC units (product returns). (PAGE 24)

counterweights.text: Genuine research pedigree: licensed UGM patents/designs, INA-SHUNT, GAMA-CHA (first halal bone graft), locally made ventilators; multiple MoH/Kemenperin/AABI awards and 20 own trademarks (PAGE 57, 58, 289-292, 315-316)
Full regulatory stack for a company this size: CPAKB, CDAKB, ISO 13485:2016, CPOTB Full Aspek, ISO 22000, halal; 13+ Kemenkes AKD device licences (PAGE 64, 65, 69-75, 313, 326)
Clean legal record: no litigation, disputes or somasi; unmodified audit opinion; labour compliance (BPJS, UMP, LKS Bipartit) (PAGE 313, 364-365)
Balance sheet: no bank debt; liabilities are affiliate loans (Rp8.3bn GMUM at 9.1% to 2030, Rp10bn YUGM at 3%), with Rp12bn to be repaid from IPO; equity Rp17.3bn (PAGE 24, 25, 29, 21, 22)
Policy tailwind: government import-substitution/localisation push for medical devices and 8% domestic market CAGR; company has already exhibited at Medical Fair Thailand (PAGE 325, 326)
Distribution agreements in place with Phapros (state pharma group) and ~20 other distributors/hospitals; own CDAKB distribution unit IMEDEV (PAGE 178-260, 321)
Independent commissioner and audit-committee chair Parsudi has BPKP/audit background; audit-committee member Richard Adikarta has listed-company experience (PAGE 297, 301)

open_questions: What is the Rp2.58bn of FY2025 revenue sold to UGM itself (36% of sales at roughly 20% gross margin): a one-off project, or something that recurs?
Excluding the impairment write-backs, what is the run-rate operating loss and cash burn, and how many years does the Rp15.8bn working-capital allocation buy?
What is the Rp37.6bn of Heprogama raw-material inventory physically, what is it worth today, and why was Rp12bn of impairment reversed over two years on stock the prospectus calls unsellable?
Why does the prospectus say no customer dominates when Phapros alone is 48% of FY2025 revenue and the top two were 89% in FY2024?
Why raise public money to repay a Rp10bn Yayasan UGM loan taken in February 2026 for land that cannot yet be transferred (65% of it is protected paddy under a conversion moratorium)?
What drove the ventilator sales collapse in 2025, and is there an order book for 2026?
After the IPO, GMUM's remaining Rp6bn loan at 9.1% stays on the books. With negative operating cash flow, how is it serviced?
Final offer price and issuance cost are blank in the draft. At the Rp140 ceiling, gross proceeds exceed the Rp40bn plan by Rp5bn. Where does the surplus go?
Will UGM add an independent director or a second independent commissioner, and what will management be paid after listing (the board drew nothing in 2024, 2025 and early 2026)?

narrativeMd:
# SWAP — PT Swayasa Prakarsa Tbk

Universitas Gadjah Mada's research-commercialisation manufacturer (medical devices, herbal, F&B) in Sleman, Yogyakarta. Upcoming IDX IPO (listing 10 Sep 2026), sole lead underwriter PT Sukadana Prima Sekuritas (formerly OSO Sekuritas). Small-asset issuer under POJK 53/2017.

- **Offering:** up to 323,000,000 new shares (100% primary) = 30.30% of post-IPO capital (1,066,000,000 shares). Par Rp20, price Rp130–140, gross Rp41.99–45.22bn; the Rp40.0bn use-of-proceeds plan implies ~Rp2–5bn undisclosed surplus/cost. No ESA, no warrants.
- **Control:** Universitas Gadjah Mada 69.60% post-IPO (67.72% via PT Gama Multi Usaha Mandiri, 98.63% UGM-owned, + 1.88% direct); the sitting Rector, Prof. dr. Ova Emilia, is the named controlling party. 8-month statutory lock (POJK 25/2017) on all four pre-IPO holders; UGM control commitment only 12 months.
- **Business:** Heprogama medical devices 80.3% of FY2025 revenue (INA-SHUNT hydrocephalus shunt, GAMA-CHA bone graft, Ceraspon, Venindo ventilators), Gamafood 18.9%, Gama Herbal 0.8%. Products are made under UGM patent/trademark licences (5% royalty). Phapros 47.8% + Anugerah Prima Medika 19.0% of revenue; UGM itself bought 36.2%.
- **Financials (audited, full Rp):** Revenue Rp10.21bn (2024) → 7.12bn (2025, −30%); FY2023 not presented. Gross profit Rp3.27bn (2025) sits below opex Rp5.45bn — an operating loss of Rp2.18bn. Net profit Rp3.46bn → 1.42bn exists only through GeNose inventory-impairment reversals (Rp6.70bn / 5.33bn); 2M-2026 net loss Rp571m; CFO negative every period. Equity Rp17.9bn; DER 0.87 (2025) → ~0.24 post-IPO.
- **Use of proceeds (Rp40.0bn net):** working capital 39.5%, new Kalasan building 30.5%, debt repayment 30.0% — the entire Rp12bn of debt repaid goes to UGM affiliates (Yayasan UGM Rp10bn, GMUM Rp2bn).
- **Valuation:** post-IPO cap Rp138.6–149.2bn; trailing FY2025 P/E 97.5–105.0× (TTM ~76–82×; n/m ex-recoveries), P/S 19.5–21.0×, P/BV 2.26–2.43× post-money; ROE 7.95% → ~2.3% post-money. The prospectus's own peer table shows ~10.6× P/E / 1.36× P/BV. Dividend up to 20% of net profit from FY2025.

See the structured cards and the full forensic writeup for the analysis. Figures from the preliminary prospectus (Prospektus Awal, 14 Aug 2026 audit report); underwriting fees, issuance cost and final price are blank in the draft.

valuation.verdict:
**Rich.** At Rp158 to 189 you pay 77 to 92 times the last twelve months' profit for a coal contractor that earned a 3.9% margin over that period and had one customer until this year.

- Market cap Rp1.05 to 1.26tn. FY2025 net profit was Rp5.1bn (205 to 245x); the twelve months to June 2026 made Rp13.7bn, and Rp5.2bn of the first half came from an affiliate paying to cancel a rental contract.
- The one year that earned a real margin, FY2023 (Rp66.9bn, 12.9%), puts the price at 16 to 19x. Profit then fell 98% in FY2024 when the sole customer's mine plan was approved late and heavy rain brought a landslide and washed out a bridge.
- On assets it is less stretched: 2.15 to 2.33x post-money book and about 8 to 9x TTM EV/EBITDA. That leaves you paying for a backlog of contracts signed in 2026, several with affiliates, that have no audited track record yet.
- Insiders put in Rp39.5bn at Rp10 a share in January 2026, a month before the six-month window that would have locked them up. Their 74.9% of the company can be sold from listing day.

dividendPolicy: After the IPO management intends to pay cash dividends of up to 30% of current-year net profit, subject to financial condition, business results and expansion plans; interim dividends are permitted under UUPT with Board of Commissioners approval; the company says it has no negative covenants restricting dividends (but bank covenants have restricted them: Mandiri/BRI/BNI/BPR clauses were waived or lifted by letters in 2026, and BCA allows dividends only while financial covenants are met). forensicMd:
## Thesis

ANDA is a coal contractor that worked for one mine owner for six years, saw its profit fall from Rp66.9bn to Rp1.2bn when that owner's mine plan slipped, and is now raising up to Rp317bn to pay down debt and fund a book of contracts signed this year. The new contracts are real and the customer list is broadening fast. But the price, Rp1.05–1.26tn, assumes those contracts already deliver, when the audited record is a 3.9% margin over the last twelve months, covenants breached at four banks, and a current ratio of 0.70. The insiders who will own three-quarters of the company bought their shares at Rp10 in January 2026, and none of them is locked up.

## How the business works

The company was incorporated in Jakarta in 2014, did nothing operational for four years (its founders never paid in their capital, a gap ratified only in March 2026), and became a mining contractor in August 2018, when current controller Billy Theristine Lim took over as President Director and signed a coal-mining services agreement with PT Budi Gema Gempita (BGG) in Lahat, South Sumatra. It removes overburden, digs and hauls coal and maintains haul roads, billed per bank cubic metre, per tonne or per tonne-kilometre, with a fleet of 33 excavators, 112 trucks and 41 support units that is largely financed or pledged. It also rents equipment with operators. Headcount is 762, almost all at the sites.

BGG was 100% of revenue in FY2023 and FY2024 and 94% in FY2025. The agreement runs "seven years from signing", which is August 2025 if counted from 2018 or about 2029 if counted from the January 2022 addendum; the prospectus gives neither an expiry date nor a renewal, and its stated contract value (Rp87.7bn) is a quarter of one year's BGG billings. In the first half of 2026 BGG revenue roughly halved year on year to Rp104.5bn, and its share fell to 52% as new work arrived: a Petrosea subcontract at PT Daya Bumindo Karunia's Murung Raya concession (Rp991.7bn to December 2029, 15% of revenue), production support for PT Satria Bahana Sarana at Tanjung Enim (Rp208.9bn to 2029, 13%), nickel ore-getting for PT Position in Halmahera Timur, an exclusive contract with PT Intan Bumi Persada to 2030, and five-year contracts with two related parties, PT Arkara Prathama Energi in Kutai Timur and PT Bukit Bara Alam in Lahat. None of these has a full year in the audited accounts, and the prospectus discloses no production volumes, utilisation or historical rates.

## The offering & ownership

Up to 1,676,000,000 new shares, 100% primary, at Rp158–189 (par Rp10) for 25.10% of a 6,676,000,000-share company: Rp264.8–316.8bn gross. Every seven new shares carry one free Series I warrant (up to 239,429,000), exercisable from June 2027 to December 2028 at Rp695, which is 3.7 to 4.4 times the offer price; the draft gives three different warrant counts and never explains the exercise price. PT Henan Putihrai Sekuritas is sole lead on full commitment, with the syndicate, fees and issuance costs still blank. The listing is on the Development Board.

Billy Theristine Lim is the designated sole controller and beneficial owner: 30% direct before the IPO (22.47% after) and about 33% effective through stakes in two holding companies. Her partner Ivan Victor owns 51% of PT Bumi Artha Caraka and 99% of PT Arkara Danatama Nusantara, which hold 37.44% between them after the IPO, yet he is not described as a controller. Those two vehicles were incorporated in December 2024 and March 2025 with Rp2.5bn of capital each and each paid Rp12.5bn into ANDA in January 2026, at Rp10 a share, alongside PT Bhumi Caraka Persada (controlled by commissioner Freddy Hartono) and Billy herself: Rp39.5bn in all, with no share premium and no disclosed source of funds. That payment landed about four weeks before the six-month look-back from the August 2026 filing, so POJK 25/2017 locks up no one. All 5.0bn pre-IPO shares, 74.9% of the company, can be sold from listing day; the only undertaking is Billy's promise not to give up control for twelve months.

## Governance & related parties

The board was rebuilt for the IPO. The audit committee, internal audit unit and corporate secretary were all created on 3 March 2026; two of five commissioners are independent and there is no independent director. The President Director, Gahari Christine, is the controller's younger sibling. The head of internal audit is concurrently GM Finance of the "Arkara Group" of companies around the controllers.

The counterparties are the same people. PT Arkara Prathama Energi, now a customer to 2030, was run by Ivan Victor until 2026, counts Billy among its commissioners, and gives a corporate and cash-deficit guarantee on ANDA's Rp203bn Mandiri loan. PT Bukit Bara Alam, a customer to 2031, is run by commissioner Freddy Hartono, and in the first half of 2026 it paid ANDA Rp5.17bn to cancel an equipment rental. PT Andalan Bhumi Nusantara, under common control, rents equipment in both directions. Billy, Ivan and Freddy pledge shares of their other companies to Mandiri, Billy and two others give personal guarantees, and Billy lent the company Rp64bn interest-free, all repaid in the same half-year the new equity arrived. Counsel declines to opine on whether the affiliate contracts are at arm's length, and a September 2026 energy-ministry decree now requires ministerial approval for new affiliate mining-service contracts. The legal opinion is otherwise clean on litigation, tax and labour; spatial-use approvals are pending at three sites and the mining-services licence expires in December 2027.

## Reading the financials

Revenue fell from Rp517.0bn (FY2023) to Rp415.4bn and then Rp368.8bn, and first-half 2026 revenue was down 8.7% to Rp200.1bn. FY2023 was the only year with a real margin: Rp66.9bn net, 12.9%. In FY2024 BGG's annual mine plan was approved only in late January, heavy rain caused a landslide and washed out a bridge, and fuel climbed to 32% of revenue, while depreciation kept rising on Rp218bn of equipment bought that year; net profit fell 98% to Rp1.2bn. FY2025 net profit of Rp5.1bn includes a Rp5.26bn insurance claim. First-half 2026 net profit of Rp11.8bn includes the Rp5.17bn Bukit Bara Alam compensation, about a third of pre-tax profit, and the gross-margin recovery to 25.9% partly reflects principals now supplying the fuel. Over the twelve months to June 2026 the company earned Rp13.7bn on Rp349.8bn of revenue.

Operating cash flow has been positive every period (Rp116bn in FY2025), and EBITDA is around Rp160bn a year. The problem is what sits above it. Depreciation alone was Rp104.5bn in FY2025 (28% of revenue), interest-bearing debt is Rp482bn (2.04x equity, about 3x EBITDA), interest cover was 1.17x and debt-service cover 0.54x. At 30 June 2026 the company was in breach of covenants at Mandiri, BCA, BRI and BNI. Waivers tied to the IPO cover the first three, one of them dated October 2026, and Rp212.7bn of bank debt that was current at December 2025 now sits as non-current. BNI has given no waiver and tests on 31 December 2026. Cash was Rp12.5bn against Rp209.3bn of payments due within a year, and 45% of trade payables were more than 90 days overdue. Before the IPO the company sold and leased back equipment it already owned at 14–15%, and borrowed Rp15bn from another company and Rp13bn interest-free from an individual to fill the gap. Equity reached Rp236.3bn in June 2026 only because of the Rp39.5bn injection.

## Valuation

At Rp158–189 the company is worth Rp1,054.8–1,261.8bn (Rp1.09–1.31tn if every warrant is exercised). That is 205–245x FY2025 earnings, 77–92x the twelve months to June 2026, and 45–54x annualised first-half 2026 profit, which includes the affiliate compensation. Only against FY2023, the year before the collapse, does it look ordinary at 16–19x. On assets the picture is milder: 4.5–5.3x book before the money, 2.15–2.33x after it, about 3x sales, and roughly 8–9x trailing EV/EBITDA once net debt and the proceeds are counted. Return on equity was 2.8% in FY2025 and falls to about 1–3% on the enlarged equity. The prospectus offers no peer table or valuation basis; the price is whatever bookbuilding bears. Buying here means paying for the 2026 contract book before it has produced a year of audited results.

## Bottom line

There is a real business here: an eight-year operator with a heavy fleet, positive operating cash flow, and a customer list that went from one name to seven in a year, including Petrosea and a Bukit Asam subsidiary. The IPO, if fully sold at the top of the range, would repay Rp107bn of expensive debt and cut total liabilities from 2.6x equity to about 1x. Against that: one customer whose contract has no stated end date and whose billings halved this year, covenant breaches at four banks, affiliates on both sides of the new contracts, thin earnings padded by an affiliate's compensation payment and an insurance claim, and insiders sitting on 15–19x their January entry price with nothing stopping them from selling. The underwriter is leading alone for the first time after five co-led deals, four of which fell 81–87% from their early highs, and press reports say OJK fined it in October 2026 over AML controls in the 2023 CUAN allocation. Wait for audited full-year 2026 results showing the new contracts deliver margin and the BNI covenant clears. At this price, with no lock-up and a 25% float, an early sell-off by insiders is as likely as a pop.

ownership.summary: ANDA is controlled by a private coal-mining owner group, not by a conglomerate, a listed parent or a politician. Billy Theristine Lim (22.47% direct post-IPO; 44.25% effective pre-IPO) is the designated controller, but her partner Ivan Victor holds about 37.5% pre-IPO (~28.1% post) through two holding companies, and the two together keep ~61% after the IPO; Freddy Hartono (~7% pre-IPO) is the third pillar. The same people sit across the table from the contractor: PT Arkara Prathama Energi (Ivan Victor CEO; Billy and Freddy commissioners) is a related-party customer and loan guarantor, and Freddy Hartono is the chief executive of new customer PT Bukit Bara Alam. About 60% of the pre-IPO shares sit in three holding vehicles formed 2023-25 that subscribed at Rp10 per share nine months before an IPO range of Rp158-189. Outside the group, the dominant customer BGG (94% of FY2025 revenue) is unrelated on paper, while the growth customer Petrosea belongs to the CUAN/Prajogo group whose IPO the sole underwriter led. We rate it family-controlled: no PEP, no IDX-listed shareholder and no foreign strategic holder found.

Oey Albert' who lent ANDA Rp18.975bn and Rp12.65bn interest-free for 36 months in Aug/Oct 2024 (Rp13.0bn outstanding at 30 Jun 2026; PAGE 288). Same name and same counterparty circle, but no document proves they are one person; if confirmed, ANDA's 94% customer's commissioner would be one of its lenders, and BGG would sit inside a listed Lampung agri group.

A local outlet (lingkaranistana.id, 2024-10-12) calls BGG 'milik konglomerat asal Lampung' and reports unresolved land-compensation disputes at its Muara Lawai (Lahat) site; no BGG ownership register was found, so the Sungai Budi attribution is inferred, not shown.

The IUP register mirror tambang.id/en/perusahaan/budi-gema-gempita/iup/batubara (accessed 2026-11-05) shows BGG's coal production IUP valid '2010-04-29 to 2026-04-29'. We could not find a renewal or the prospectus's treatment of it; the registry copy may lag, so this is a question to ask, not a finding.

The prospectus labels PT Mustika Indah Permai '(Adaro Group)' (PAGE 149), and directories (arest.web.id/content/pt-mustika-indah-permai; disnakerja.com, 2026-09-10) describe it as an Adaro-group coal miner in Lahat. Whether Freddy Hartono is an operating director or an owner there is not established; 'Hartono' is a common surname and he is not linked to any other Hartono family.

'Salim' in Ivan Victor Salim (detikNews 2024) is not linked to the Salim Group. 'Willy Christine' (60% of TLI) shares a given name with CEO Gahari Christine but is absent from the prospectus family table, so she is not treated as family. 'Tony Law' (Mandiri personal guarantor), 'Anita Rizky HP' (1% of ADN), 'Sukamdani Kencana Y' (owner of a time deposit pledged to BCA, PAGE 294) and 'Arief Ramon' could not be identified publicly.

Lender PT Batu Energi Perdana (Rp15bn, 5%, due 31 Dec 2026; PAGE 288) is named 'Batu Energi Persada' on PAGE 110; its owners are not disclosed and no link to the Batu Group mining holding was established. The controller of affiliate PT Andalan Bhumi Nusantara is not named in the prospectus.

APE received a Kutai Timur DLH environmental sanction in May 2023 (temporary halt to land clearing outside its concession plus an administrative coercive order; kabaretam.com, 2023-05-29); PT Position (nickel customer, held via Harum Energy's subsidiary) faces press allegations over Maba Sangaji indigenous-forest mining (kadera.id, 2025-08-11). Both are reputational context on counterparties, not findings against ANDA or its shareholders.

Sponsor cross-reference: OJK fined Henan Putihrai Sekuritas Rp1.7bn (S-48/PM.2/2026, 16 Oct 2026) over anti-money-laundering controls in the 2023 CUAN IPO and froze its director Jurgantara Usman's underwriter-representative licence for three months (katadata.co.id, 2026-11-02; insight.kontan.co.id, 2026-11-01); see the underwriter file. It is a sanction on the firm, not on ANDA.

inputs.label: Analyst verdict
inputs.value:
**Rich.** At Rp158 to 189 you pay 77 to 92 times the last twelve months' profit for a coal contractor that earned a 3.9% margin over that period and had one customer until this year.

- Market cap Rp1.05 to 1.26tn. FY2025 net profit was Rp5.1bn (205 to 245x); the twelve months to June 2026 made Rp13.7bn, and Rp5.2bn of the first half came from an affiliate paying to cancel a rental contract.
- The one year that earned a real margin, FY2023 (Rp66.9bn, 12.9%), puts the price at 16 to 19x. Profit then fell 98% in FY2024 when the sole customer's mine plan was approved late and heavy rain brought a landslide and washed out a bridge.
- On assets it is less stretched: 2.15 to 2.33x post-money book and about 8 to 9x TTM EV/EBITDA. That leaves you paying for a backlog of contracts signed in 2026, several with affiliates, that have no audited track record yet.
- Insiders put in Rp39.5bn at Rp10 a share in January 2026, a month before the six-month window that would have locked them up. Their 74.9% of the company can be sold from listing day.

underwriter.summary: Five joint-lead IPOs in 2023-25 (about Rp3.99T raised), each with a different co-lead; none in 2022. All five remain above offer on 5 Nov 2026 (+63% to +1,536%), but four are 81-87% below their peaks and three sit 61-66% below their D7 closes. Average D1 +28.2%, average D7 +300%. Issuers cluster in tycoon-controlled names: two Prajogo units (CUAN, CDIA), Happy Hapsoro's RATU, DAAZ and FORE.

lockup.lockup_trigger_basis: DERIVED: registration filed 2026-08-26 -> 6-month look-back starts 2026-02-26. The Rp39.5bn injection (shares issued at Rp10 per post-split share, ~16–19x below IPO price) was paid 29–30 Jan 2026 and the deed approved by Menkum 6 Feb 2026 – 20 days (payments 27–28 days) OUTSIDE the window; the TLI->Billy 150,000,000-share sale (3 Mar 2026, Rp10/share) is inside the window but is a secondary transfer, not an acquisition 'dari Perseroan'. Hence every pre-IPO share (5,000,000,000 = 74.90% post-IPO) is freely tradable from listing day on the Papan Pengembangan.

raw.dividend_policy: After the IPO management intends to pay cash dividends of up to 30% of current-year net profit, subject to financial condition, business results and expansion plans; interim dividends are permitted under UUPT with Board of Commissioners approval; the company says it has no negative covenants restricting dividends (but bank covenants have restricted them: Mandiri/BRI/BNI/BPR clauses were waived or lifted by letters in 2026, and BCA allows dividends only while financial covenants are met). The company has never paid a dividend since incorporation; the 17 Jun 2026 AGM allocated Rp2.1bn of FY2025 profit to a statutory reserve and retained the rest with no distribution. At 30% of the TTM net profit (Rp13.65bn) the payout would be ~Rp4.1bn, i.e. ~0.07% of the Rp1.26tn market cap at the Rp189 ceiling.

business.summary: PT Andalan Artha Primanusa Tbk (ANDA) is a Jakarta-based mining-services contractor: overburden/mud removal, coal getting (and, since April 2026, nickel-ore getting), coal hauling, haul-road maintenance, plus rental of heavy equipment (with or without operator). Work is won by negotiation or tender from mine-concession owners and is billed on measured volume (BCM / tonne / ton-km) or hourly/monthly equipment rates. KBLI actually performed: 09900 only. Customers are all third-party B2B mine owners; no state-funded contracts. FY2023-FY2025 revenue was essentially one customer (PT Budi Gema Gempita, BGG); the 2026 contract wave (PTRO, SBS, IBP, APE, BBA, POS, BSB) is the diversification story and is almost entirely signed Mar-Jul 2026, i.e. unproven in the audited numbers.
business.history: Established 16 Jun 2014 by Akta No. 36 (Notary Antonius Wahono Prawirodirdjo, Jakarta Utara), MenkumHAM approval AHU-17455.AH.01.01.Tahun 2014 dated 12 Aug 2014; founders Heru Sumbogo 50% / Sudiyo 50% (2,000 shares x Rp1,000,000 = Rp2bn issued of Rp5bn authorised). The prospectus says the company was 'dahulu didirikan dengan nama PT Nusa Karya Realti' (Ringkasan p.19; Bab VIII A p.98) but Bab VIII B p.164 says it was incorporated under the name 'PT Andalan Artha Primanusa' - no date, deed or reason for the rename is given anywhere. Founders' initial capital was never actually paid in: shareholders only 'menyetujui dan meratifikasi ketiadaan penyetoran modal pertama kali' by Akta No. 21 of 3 Mar 2026 (p.98). Jul-Aug 2018: PT Tambang Lancar Indonesia (d.h. PT Tower Light Indonesia) and Arief Ramon subscribed Rp3bn new shares and bought out both founders (Rp1bn each) -> 50/50 TLI/Arief; Billy Theristine Lim became Direktur Utama 31 Jul 2018 (p.139). 8 Aug 2018: first mining contract signed with BGG (Tanjung Enim, South Sumatra per history table p.103; Lahat per FS Note 28 p.64 - location inconsistency) = 'proyek operasional pertama' - i.e. the company only became a mining contractor in 2018, four years after incorporation (FS Note 1: 'memulai operasinya sejak tahun 2014'). Oct 2024: capital raised Rp5.5bn (Billy Rp4bn, TLI Rp1.5bn) -> Billy 38.1% largest holder; Series A/B share classes created (p.104-105). 16 Dec 2024: Billy moves from Dirut to Komisaris Utama (p.139). 30 Dec 2024 SBS contract; 2026: reclassification (Akta 23, 5 Feb 2026), paid-up capital raised Rp10.5bn -> Rp50bn (Rp39.5bn cash from Billy Rp9.5bn, PT Bumi Artha Caraka Rp12.5bn, PT Arkara Danatama Nusantara Rp12.5bn, PT Bhumi Caraka Persada Rp5bn - Jan 2026), POS Letter of Award 22 Jan 2026 (nickel, first non-coal commodity), TLI sells 150m shares to Billy for Rp1.5bn on 3 Mar 2026, par split to Rp10, IPO approval Akta 308 of 27 Jul 2026 (p.98-107).

model.contract_process: Contracts are obtained by direct negotiation or tender with the concession owner; scope, tariff, production target and term are fixed in the cooperation agreement; mobilisation of equipment/labour; volumes measured in BCM or metric tonnes per contract and invoiced per agreed payment terms (p.165).
model.pricing_basis: Per BCM (OB, mud, cut&fill), per tonne (coal getting), per tonne-km (hauling, road maintenance), per 100 m overdistance premium, per hour (SBS bulldozers Rp1,980,000/hr at 400 hrs/month), per month lump-sum or hourly rental (BSB, IBP, ABN). BBA contracts are USD-denominated (OB USD0.70 per unit/1,000 m; coal getting fixed USD0.7/MT + USD0.0136/100m/MT). BGG contract described as 'double rate' coal mining (p.126).
model.fuel_supplier: Fuel (BBM) was borne by ANDA on BGG-type contracts (fuel = 25% of revenue in H1 2025); on the PTRO/DBK and SBS projects fuel is supplied by the client, which cut fuel cost to ~15% of revenue in H1 2026 and mechanically lowered both revenue (no fuel pass-through) and cost of revenue (p.80, 166). BSB rental rates exclude BBM (p.67). Use-of-proceeds budget still buys fuel from Pertamina Patra Niaga, Twin Berkah Energi, Sumber Karya Anugerah, Indo Lautan Energi (non-affiliates, p.42).
model.contract_tenor: BGG: '7 tahun' from 8 Aug 2018 signing (addendum effective 1 Jan 2022) - literal reading = expired 7 Aug 2025, no extension disclosed. SBS to 29 Dec 2029; PTRO subcontract to 31 Dec 2029; POS 4 years from 1 Apr 2026; IBP and APE to 31 Dec 2030 (IBP subject to IUP-OP renewal); BBA 1 Sep 2026 - 31 Aug 2031; rentals (ABN, BSB) 1 Jan - 31 Dec 2026.
model.no_escalation_disclosed: Only mitigant stated is that management 'mengupayakan pencantuman mekanisme penyesuaian tarif (cost escalation atau rise and fall)' (p.157) - i.e. no contractual escalation is confirmed in the contract summaries.

revenue_breakdown.by_commodity: Coal = 100% of revenue FY2023-FY2025. Nickel (POS, Halmahera Timur) effective 1 Apr 2026 - first revenue falls in H1 2026 (117 'Ore Getting - Nickel' employees at 30 Jun 2026, p.162) but the prospectus gives NO Rp or % split between coal and nickel. H1 2026 revenue declined 8.68% to Rp200.12bn (-Rp19.04bn) 'murni' due to price-structure change as production shifted to DBK/SBS where the client supplies fuel (p.166, 79-80).

risk_factors.text: PRIMARY: Dependence on main employer (BGG). Revenue concentration; risk of lower production targets, delayed receivables, unilateral termination or non-renewal. BGG = 100% (2024), 94.03% (2025), 52.25% (H1 2026) of revenue; contract tenor ambiguity (7 yrs from 8 Aug 2018 -> literal expiry Aug 2025, no extension shown).
Reduction in production volume from employer RKAB adjustments (ESDM production quota changes) - lowers contractor volume and margin.
Weather and natural disasters (rainfall, flooding, landslides) halting pit and hauling operations; nickel haulage in Halmahera also exposed.
Equipment breakdown / physical availability - unscheduled failures, age of fleet, lost billable hours in rental; BSB contract penalises PA <85% / MA <80%.
Human resources - SIO-certified operators and POP supervisors scarce, turnover, productivity; headcount to double vs 762 to serve 7 sites.
Operating cost risk - fuel price, rupiah depreciation (equipment & spares), minimum wage; fuel was 25% of revenue in H1 2025 on fuel-supplied contracts; no contractual escalation confirmed.

Ability to meet cash payment obligations - DSCR 0.86x, not enough operating cash flow to cover principal and interest, 'dapat mempengaruhi kelangsungan usaha (going concern)'; covenant breaches (Debt/EBITDA 2.69x, DER 2.04, CR 0.70); BNI waiver not obtained.
Commodity price fluctuation lowers employers' targets and delays mine development (prospectus management section claims 'tidak ada dampak langsung' - internally contradictory).
Competition - tariff pressure from incumbents (PTRO, UNTR, DOID, DEWA, RMKO, MINE).
Non-renewal of IUJP (valid to Dec 2027); renewal application planned by 8 Dec 2026; non-renewal could stop operations temporarily or permanently.
Investment or corporate-action risk - no guarantee of success of expansion/corporate actions.
General: changes in mining policy (UU 3/2020, RKAB approvals, environmental obligations) affecting IUP-holder customers.
General: macro and global conditions - inflation, rupiah, interest rates, tighter funding of employers' capex.
Investors: Indonesian capital-market liquidity and volatility; limited float (Papan Pengembangan).
Investors: possible change/non-realisation of use-of-proceeds (POJK 40/2025 rules apply).

Investors: dividend policy constrained by cash flow, covenants and capex; no dividend ever paid since 2014.

raw.primary_business_risk: Dependence on one mine owner: PT Budi Gema Gempita supplied 100% of revenue in FY2023-24, 94% in FY2025 and 52% in 6M2026; its contract's seven-year term has no stated expiry date or renewal, and most replacement contracts were signed in 2026 and have no audited track record (PAGE 1, 92, 126, 312).
raw.industry_tailwind: The prospectus cites IEA data that Asian coal consumption stays the main support of global demand in the medium term, led by China and India, and PLN's RUPTL 2025-2034, which projects electricity demand growth of 5.3% a year, 69,512 MW of planned capacity (42,569 MW renewable + 10,256 MW storage + 16,687 MW fossil), and coal still at ~73% of the 2026 generation mix and ~52% in 2034 (renewable target 34.3% in 2034). It adds that government production-quota policy (RKAB) may limit mine owners' output and thus contractor volumes, but that Indonesian miners generally outsource overburden removal, mining and hauling to third-party contractors. For nickel it cites Indonesia as >60% of global mined nickel in 2024 and 67% of mining supply per IEA, export value USD9.73bn in 2025 (COMTRADE), global demand +6% to 3.4mt in 2024, energy-technology share ~20% (2024) rising to >40% by 2040, but also a short-term surplus, nickel at ~USD17,200/t in March, an Indonesian ore quota of 260-270m wmt for 2026, and smelter utilisation of ~70-75%, and 75% of smelter sulphur reliant on Middle East supply. Management concludes coal contractor prospects are 'stabil, moderat dan selektif' for 2026-2027 and nickel contractor prospects 'tetap positif'. [All data are third-party/management statements in the prospectus; none is independently verified here.]

valuation.verdict:
**Rich.** At Rp158 to 189 you pay 77 to 92 times the last twelve months' profit for a coal contractor that earned a 3.9% margin over that period and had one customer until this year.

- Market cap Rp1.05 to 1.26tn. FY2025 net profit was Rp5.1bn (205 to 245x); the twelve months to June 2026 made Rp13.7bn, and Rp5.2bn of the first half came from an affiliate paying to cancel a rental contract.
- The one year that earned a real margin, FY2023 (Rp66.9bn, 12.9%), puts the price at 16 to 19x. Profit then fell 98% in FY2024 when the sole customer's mine plan was approved late and heavy rain brought a landslide and washed out a bridge.
- On assets it is less stretched: 2.15 to 2.33x post-money book and about 8 to 9x TTM EV/EBITDA. That leaves you paying for a backlog of contracts signed in 2026, several with affiliates, that have no audited track record yet.
- Insiders put in Rp39.5bn at Rp10 a share in January 2026, a month before the six-month window that would have locked them up. Their 74.9% of the company can be sold from listing day.

red_flags.flag: Single-customer history: PT Budi Gema Gempita (BGG) was 100% of revenue in FY2023 (Rp517.0bn) and FY2024 (Rp415.4bn) and 94% in FY2025 (Rp348.0bn); BGG revenue roughly halved y/y in 6M2026 (Rp212.6bn -> Rp104.5bn) and total revenue fell 29% from FY2023 to FY2025. The prospectus names dependence on its main customer as the primary risk (PAGE 1, 84, 92, 174, 312)

BGG contract expiry is unclear: the agreement 'berlaku untuk jangka waktu 7 (tujuh) tahun terhitung sejak tanggal ditandatanganinya', which ends in Aug 2025 if counted from the 8 Aug 2018 signing or around Jan 2029 if counted from the 2022 addendum. No expiry date, renewal, termination right, rate basis or order book is given, and the stated value (Rp87.7bn) is a quarter of one year's BGG revenue (PAGE 64, 126)

Covenants breached at all four banks on 30 Jun 2026: Mandiri DSCR 0.86x vs 1.25x, Debt/EBITDA 2.69x vs 2.0x, DER 2.04x vs 2.0x; BCA DSC and current ratio 0.70x vs 1.0x; BRI DSCR vs 1.1x; BNI current ratio and DSC with no waiver, tested on 31 Dec 2026. Waivers are tied to the IPO and one (Mandiri, 7 Oct 2026) post-dates the balance sheet, which is what lets Rp212.7bn of debt sit as non-current (PAGE 25, 26, 57, 73, 74, 337)

Thin liquidity: current ratio 0.70x, negative working capital of Rp100.2bn and Rp12.5bn of cash against Rp209.3bn of debt and lease payments due within 12 months; 45% of trade payables (Rp33.7bn) are more than 90 days overdue; DSCR was 0.54x in FY2025 (PAGE 24, 25, 45, 50, 70, 91)

No lock-up on any pre-IPO holder: the prospectus states no shareholder is barred under POJK 25/2017, so all 5.0bn pre-IPO shares (74.90% post-IPO) can be sold from listing day. The Rp39.5bn injection at Rp10 a share was paid on 29-30 Jan 2026, about four weeks before the six-month look-back from the 26 Aug 2026 filing begins; the only undertaking is Billy Theristine Lim's 12-month no-change-of-control pledge (PAGE 38, 105-107, 209)

Insiders entered at Rp10 a share, 15.8-18.9x below the IPO range: 90% of the Rp50bn paid-up capital arrived in the last two years at par (Sep 2024 Rp5.5bn; Jan 2026 Rp39.5bn, no share premium). PT Bumi Artha Caraka (incorporated Mar 2025) and PT Arkara Danatama Nusantara (Dec 2024) each paid Rp12.5bn with Rp2.5bn of their own capital; the source of the funds is not disclosed (PAGE 105, 106, 140-145, 238, 309)

Earnings are thin and padded by one-offs: TTM net profit Rp13.65bn on Rp349.8bn revenue (3.9% margin). FY2025 net profit Rp5.14bn includes a Rp5.26bn insurance claim (pre-tax ex-claim ~Rp1.4bn); 6M2026 profit Rp11.77bn includes Rp5.17bn of compensation from affiliate PT Bukit Bara Alam for cancelling an equipment rental, about a third of pre-tax profit (PAGE 78, 79, 317, 318)

Related-party web around the controllers: new customers PT Arkara Prathama Energi (ANDA's Komut and CEO hold posts there) and PT Bukit Bara Alam (an ANDA commissioner is its director; five-year contracts signed 9 Jul 2026) and equipment counterparty PT Andalan Bhumi Nusantara (common control). Counsel declines to opine on arm's length, and ESDM Kepmen 365/2026 now requires ministerial approval for new affiliate mining-service contracts (PAGE 108, 109, 139, 149, 214, 215, 316)

Control is understated on paper: Billy Theristine Lim is the designated sole controller with 22.47% direct post-IPO, while Ivan Victor owns 51% of PT Bumi Artha Caraka and 99% of PT Arkara Danatama Nusantara, which together hold 37.44% post-IPO; he is not described as a controller anywhere (PAGE 9, 139-145, 210)

Leverage: total liabilities 2.63x equity at Jun 2026 (2.91x FY2025), interest-bearing debt Rp482.2bn = 2.04x equity and ~3.0x TTM EBITDA; interest cover 1.17x in FY2025. Pro forma ~1.0x only if the full Rp280-306bn of new equity arrives (PAGE 24, 25, 45-63, 70)

Use-of-proceeds Rupiah amounts only hold at the Rp189 ceiling with every share sold: at Rp158 net proceeds fall to ~Rp253.8bn and the 35% debt tranche to ~Rp88.8bn. The stated working-capital need is Rp607bn against Rp198.7bn raised, with Series I warrant cash (exercise Rp695, 3.7-4.4x the offer price) named as the second funding source (PAGE 39-44)

Pre-IPO cash squeeze: equipment the company already owned was sale-and-leased-back to Radana Bhaskara Finance at 14-15% (Rp40.5bn Aug 2025, Rp25.0bn Mar 2026), plus a Rp15bn loan from PT Batu Energi Perdana (Jun 2026), a Rp13bn interest-free loan from an undescribed individual and Rp16bn from shareholder Arief Ramon; the IPO repays Radana but none of these (PAGE 39, 40, 51, 62, 63, 316)

Governance is eight months old: audit committee, internal audit and corporate secretary all formed 3 Mar 2026; no independent director; 2 of 5 commissioners independent; the CEO is the controller's younger sibling; the head of internal audit is concurrently GM Finance of the 'Arkara Group' around the controllers (PAGE 145-155; family-relationship table PAGE 150)

Auditor change and an unexplained emphasis of matter: FY2023-24 were audited by KAP Griselda, Wisnu dan Arum with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph whose text the prospectus never reproduces; BDO's firm was appointed on 2 Jul 2026 for FY2025 and 6M2026 (PAGE 23, 45, 183, 341, 343)

Licensing gaps at the new sites: PKKPR (spatial-use approval) still pending at three customer sites (IBP, DBK, APE) as of 19 Oct 2026 though work has started; the IUJP mining-services licence expires 8 Dec 2027 (PAGE 107, 211, 212)
Heavy-equipment insurance cover fell from Rp521.6bn (Dec 2025) to Rp294.0bn (Jun 2026) while the fleet is fully pledged to banks and lessors (PAGE 60, 130)

Unfinished, internally inconsistent draft: issuance costs, fee split, syndicate and pro-forma equity are blank; the warrant count appears as 239.4m, 485.7m and 558.7m; bookbuilding is described in the past tense in a prospectus dated the day it starts; founders' 2014 capital was never paid in and was ratified only in Mar 2026 (PAGE 1, 44, 98, 99, 176, 181, 310)

counterweights.text: Customer base is diversifying fast: BGG fell from 94% of revenue (FY2025) to 52% (6M2026) with PT Petrosea Tbk 15% and PT Satria Bahana Sarana (a PTBA subsidiary) 13%, both established counterparties, plus ~20% from new sites; mining-segment operating margin rose from 8.9% to 16.0% and group gross margin to 25.9% (PAGE 78-85, 312)

Multi-year contracts signed in 2026: Petrosea subcontract Rp991.7bn to Dec 2029, SBS Rp208.9bn to Dec 2029, exclusive IBP to 2030, PT Position nickel ore-getting (4 years), BBA to 2031 - visibility if they are executed (PAGE 64-68, 108, 109, 126, 127)

Operating cash flow positive every period presented: Rp151.9bn (FY2023), Rp60.9bn (FY2024), Rp116.1bn (FY2025), Rp26.4bn (6M2026); trade receivables Rp73.4bn with nothing over 90 days at Jun 2026 (PAGE 239, 273, 317)

100% primary, and 35% of net proceeds retires 9.5-15% debt (Radana in full Rp65.0bn, Mandiri Rp42.0bn), cutting roughly Rp12-13bn of annual interest and taking total liabilities/equity from 2.63x to ~1.0x pro forma (PAGE 21, 39-41)

Controller has cash in and is tied to the lenders: the Rp64bn interest-free shareholder loan was repaid in 6M2026, Rp39.5bn of new equity went in, Billy Theristine Lim personally guarantees the Mandiri loan and banks require her effective stake to stay above ~20.7% (PAGE 47, 66, 238, 316, 337)

Real asset base: 33 excavators, 112 trucks and 41 support units; PPE net Rp436.4bn plus right-of-use Rp165.8bn; BDO's key audit matter found no impairment indicator after physical inspection (PAGE 129, 278, 342)
Clean legal opinion on litigation, tax and labour for the company and its board; 762 permanent employees; eight years without a fatality claimed (PAGE 161-166, 211)

Why is the Series I warrant exercise price Rp695, 3.7 to 4.4 times the offer price, and which warrant count (239.4m, 485.7m or 558.7m) is correct?

narrativeMd:
# ANDA — PT Andalan Artha Primanusa Tbk

Jakarta-based coal (and since 2026 nickel) mining contractor: overburden removal, coal getting and hauling with an owned and leased fleet of 33 excavators and 112 trucks, plus heavy-equipment rental. Upcoming IDX IPO (listing 1 Dec 2026, Papan Pengembangan), sole lead underwriter PT Henan Putihrai Sekuritas on full commitment.

- **Offering:** up to 1,676,000,000 new shares (100% primary) = 25.10% of post-IPO capital (6,676,000,000 shares). Par Rp10, price Rp158–189, gross Rp264.8–316.8bn. Free Series I warrants, 1 per 7 new shares (up to 239,429,000), exercise Rp695 (3.7–4.4× the offer range), exercisable 1 Jun 2027 – 1 Dec 2028, up to Rp166.4bn. No ESA. Issuance costs blank in the draft; the use-of-proceeds Rupiah amounts back-solve to Rp305.7bn net at the Rp189 ceiling (3.48% cost).
- **Control:** Ny. Billy Theristine Lim, Komisaris Utama, is the designated sole controller and beneficial owner: 22.47% direct post-IPO, ~33.1% effective via 49% of PT Bumi Artha Caraka and 40% of PT Tambang Lancar Indonesia. Ivan Victor owns 51% of Bumi Artha Caraka and 99% of PT Arkara Danatama Nusantara (together 37.44% post-IPO). CEO Gahari Christine is the controller's younger sibling. **No POJK 25/2017 lock-up applies to anyone**: the Rp39.5bn injection at Rp10/share (Jan 2026) was paid just before the six-month look-back. Only a 12-month no-change-of-control pledge.
- **Business:** PT Budi Gema Gempita was 100% of revenue in FY2023–24 and 94% in FY2025; in 6M2026 it fell to 52% as Petrosea (15%), Satria Bahana Sarana (13%) and new sites (~20%) came on. Seven contracts signed in 2026 run to 2029–2031 (Petrosea subcontract Rp991.7bn, SBS Rp208.9bn, PT Position nickel, IBP, and affiliates Arkara Prathama Energi and Bukit Bara Alam). The BGG contract runs "seven years from signing" with no stated expiry: Aug 2025 from the 2018 agreement, ~2029 from the 2022 addendum.
- **Financials (audited, full Rp):** Revenue Rp517.0bn (2023) → 415.4bn (2024) → 368.8bn (2025); 6M2026 Rp200.1bn (−8.7% y/y). Net profit Rp66.9bn → 1.2bn → 5.1bn; 6M2026 Rp11.8bn (incl. Rp5.17bn affiliate compensation); FY2025 includes a Rp5.26bn insurance claim. TTM to Jun-2026: revenue Rp349.8bn, net profit Rp13.7bn, EBITDA ~Rp160bn. CFO positive every period. Equity Rp236.3bn (Jun 2026); total liabilities/equity 2.63×, interest-bearing debt Rp482bn (2.04×), current ratio 0.70×, DSCR 0.86× — covenants breached at Mandiri, BCA, BRI and BNI (BNI unwaived, tested 31 Dec 2026).
- **Use of proceeds (Rp305.7bn net at ceiling):** 35% debt — Radana Bhaskara Finance leases repaid in full (Rp65.0bn, 11.4–15%) and Bank Mandiri investment credit in part (Rp42.0bn, 9.5%); 65% working capital (fuel 20.1%, field wages 31.0%, spare parts/lubricants/tyres 13.9%). Nothing to affiliates. Warrant cash, if any, also goes to working capital.
- **Valuation:** post-IPO cap Rp1,054.8–1,261.8bn. Trailing FY2025 P/E 205–245×, TTM 77–92×; FY2023-peak P/E 16–19×. P/BV 4.5–5.3× pre-money, 2.15–2.33× post-money; P/S 2.9–3.4×; EV/TTM EBITDA ~7.9–8.9×. ROE 2.8% (FY2025) → ~1.1% post-money (2.7% on TTM). No peer table or valuation basis in the prospectus. Dividend up to 30% of net profit; never paid.

See the structured cards and the forensic writeup for the analysis. Figures from the preliminary prospectus (Prospektus Awal, 5 Nov 2026; BDO audit report 23 Oct 2026); final price, fees and syndicate are blank in the draft.
